description: Coast redwoods reach over 110m. The tallest known tree's location is deliberately unpublished to protect the ground around its roots.

title: Walk across the Golden Gate Bridge
description: 2.7km of art deco steel painted International Orange so it stays visible in fog. September and October are the clearest months.

title: Take the night tour of Alcatraz
description: A federal prison for 29 years, and occupied by Native American activists for 19 months from 1969 - graffiti from that occupation is still on the walls.

title: Ride a cable car up Hyde Street
description: The last manually operated cable car system in the world, running since 1873 by gripping a cable moving under the street at a constant 15km/h.

title: Walk among the old-growth at Muir Woods
description: One of the last uncut coast redwood stands near the coast, saved in 1908. Parking and shuttle must be reserved in advance - no walk-ups.

title: Taste Cabernet in the Napa Valley
description: The 1976 Judgement of Paris, where Napa beat Bordeaux blind, remade the region. Most tastings now need a booking.

title: See the city from Griffith Observatory
description: Free since it opened in 1935, with the Hollywood sign on one side and the whole basin on the other. Go at dusk and stay for the telescope.

title: Walk the Venice Beach boardwalk
description: Built in 1905 as a Californian imitation of Venice, canals included. Now street performers, Muscle Beach and a skate park on the sand.

title: See the tar pits at La Brea
description: Asphalt still seeping in the middle of Los Angeles, having trapped and preserved Ice Age animals for 50,000 years. Excavation continues on site.

title: Kayak the sea caves at La Jolla
description: Seven caves cut into the sandstone cliff, in a marine reserve with leopard sharks in the shallows through summer and sea lions on the rocks.

title: Spend a day in Balboa Park
description: 490 hectares of Spanish Colonial Revival buildings from the 1915 exposition, holding 17 museums and the San Diego Zoo.

title: Swim in Lake Tahoe
description: 501m deep and clear enough to see 20m down, straddling the California and Nevada line. Cold enough that most people manage about four minutes.

title: Look into Crater Lake
description: The deepest lake in the US at 594m, filling a caldera left when Mount Mazama collapsed about 7,700 years ago. Fed only by rain and snow.

title: Walk up to Multnomah Falls
description: 189m in two drops with a 1914 footbridge across the middle. Timed-entry permits apply in summer - book before you drive out.

title: Watch the tide come in at Haystack Rock
description: A 72m sea stack with tufted puffins nesting on it in spring and tide pools at its base. Oregon beaches are public and dog friendly by law.

title: Watch the sea drain into Thor's Well
description: A collapsed sea cave that appears to swallow the ocean. Best an hour either side of high tide - and people have been swept off these rocks.

title: See the Painted Hills change colour
description: Banded claystone recording 35 million years of climate change, and the colours genuinely shift with moisture and light through the day.

title: Climb Misery Ridge at Smith Rock
description: The birthplace of American sport climbing, on welded tuff above a river bend. The ridge trail is short, steep and named accurately.

title: Get lost in Powell's City of Books
description: A city block of new and used books shelved side by side - around a million of them, and the largest independent bookshop in the world.

title: Walk the Hoh Rain Forest in Olympic
description: A temperate rainforest getting up to 4 metres of rain a year, with moss hanging off every branch - and glaciers and coast in the same park.

title: Walk through Hole-in-the-Wall at Rialto Beach
description: Driftwood logs the size of telegraph poles, sea stacks in the mist, and an arch you can only reach at low tide. Check the tide table, seriously.

title: See the wildflowers at Paradise on Mount Rainier
description: An active volcano carrying more glacial ice than the rest of the lower 48 combined, with a six-week meadow bloom at its foot.

title: Watch the fish throwers at Pike Place Market
description: Trading since 1907, and one of the oldest continuously operating farmers markets in the country. The first Starbucks is across the street.

title: Look for resident orcas in the San Juan Islands
description: The Southern Resident orcas are down to about 73 animals and no longer reliably here - transient Bigg's killer whales are now the more likely sighting.

title: Stand above Palouse Falls
description: A 60m fall into a basalt bowl carved by the Missoula floods at the end of the last ice age. Best in spring melt, and the cliff edges are unfenced.

title: Take the bus into Denali
description: One 148km road into six million acres, and private vehicles are barred beyond mile 15. Grizzly, caribou, moose and wolf all along it.

title: Chase the northern lights from Fairbanks
description: Sitting under the auroral oval, with displays on roughly four nights in five when skies are clear between September and March.

title: Watch tidewater glaciers calve in Kenai Fjords
description: Nearly 40 glaciers flow off the Harding Icefield, several straight into the sea - the boat cuts its engines and you listen to the ice crack.

title: Watch bears fish at Brooks Falls
description: Brown bears catching salmon mid-air from a viewing platform in Katmai. Reachable only by float plane, and the subject of Fat Bear Week.

title: Cruise into Glacier Bay
description: Entirely covered by ice in 1794 and now open water for 100km - one of the fastest documented glacial retreats anywhere. Huna Tlingit homeland.

title: Drive the Dalton Highway to the Arctic Circle
description: 666km of mostly gravel built to service the oil pipeline, with three fuel stops on the entire route and no mobile coverage.

title: Ride the Alaska Railroad to Seward
description: Four hours from Anchorage through country with no road access at all, and one of the last railways anywhere you can flag down from the trackside.

title: Watch Kilauea glow after dark
description: One of the most active volcanoes on earth. Whether there is anything to see depends entirely on the current eruption - check the USGS status first.

title: Stargaze from Mauna Kea
description: 4,207m and the best-placed observatory site on earth. It is also sacred to Native Hawaiians, and telescope construction here remains contested.

title: Walk down to Papakolea green sand beach
description: One of only a handful of green sand beaches in the world, coloured by olivine from an eroding cinder cone. A hot 8km round trip on foot.

title: Watch sunrise from the Haleakala summit
description: 3,055m above the clouds, and about 3C at dawn. Sunrise entry needs a reservation booked up to 60 days ahead - there is no walk-up option.

title: Drive the Road to Hana
description: 620 curves and 59 one-lane bridges in 84km. Locals still use this road daily - pull over and let them past.

title: Snorkel the Molokini crater
description: A sunken volcanic crescent forming a sheltered crater with 45m visibility, and a marine reserve since 1977.

title: See the Na Pali Coast from the water
description: 27km of 1,200m cliffs with no road access at all. Boat, helicopter, or the Kalalau Trail - and that trail needs a permit and a head for heights.

title: Look into Waimea Canyon
description: Mark Twain reputedly called it the Grand Canyon of the Pacific - 16km long and 900m deep, cut into red volcanic rock.

title: Stand above the USS Arizona at Pearl Harbor
description: 1,177 crew died on the Arizona and most remain aboard. Oil still seeps from the wreck, a couple of drops a minute, eighty years on.

title: Learn to surf at Waikiki
description: Long, slow, forgiving waves and the beach where Duke Kahanamoku introduced surfing to the wider world. The gentlest place anywhere to start.

title: Walk the Strip after dark in Las Vegas
description: 6.8km of casinos built on a desert crossroads. Whatever you think of it, there is nowhere else quite like it, and walking it takes longer than it looks.

title: Find the petroglyphs at Valley of Fire
description: Nevada's oldest state park - Aztec sandstone in violent reds, with 3,000-year-old rock art at Atlatl Rock and the Fire Wave a short walk in.

title: See the Milky Way from Great Basin National Park
description: Some of the darkest skies left in the continental US, plus bristlecone pines that were already thousands of years old when Rome fell.

title: Drive the Extraterrestrial Highway
description: 158km of State Route 375 past the back gate of Area 51, with one small town, one bar and no fuel for long stretches.

title: Hike below the rim of the Grand Canyon
description: Going down is optional, coming back up is not - rangers pull people off the Bright Angel Trail every summer. Go in spring or autumn.

title: Reach the quieter North Rim of the Grand Canyon
description: Takes about a tenth of the visitors, sits 300m higher, and closes under snow from December. Four hours' drive from the South Rim to go 16km.

title: Raft the Colorado through the Grand Canyon
description: Up to three weeks and 440km through the canyon floor. Private permits run on a weighted lottery with a wait that has run to years.

title: Walk down to Havasu Falls
description: Turquoise water from travertine minerals, 16km down into Havasupai land. Permits sell out within minutes on the February release and are non-transferable.

title: See the light beams in Antelope Canyon
description: A slot canyon on Navajo Nation land, accessible only with a Navajo guide. The shafts of light appear around midday from about March to October.

title: Stand above Horseshoe Bend
description: A 270-degree meander of the Colorado, 300m below an unfenced sandstone rim. Twenty minutes from the car park, and no shade at all.

title: Drive the valley floor at Monument Valley
description: A Navajo tribal park, not a national park - the sandstone buttes John Ford filmed nine times. The 27km loop road is rough but doable in a normal car.

title: Win the lottery for The Wave at Coyote Buttes
description: Undulating Navajo sandstone laid down as dunes 190 million years ago. Only 64 people a day get in, by lottery, and the route is unmarked.

title: Climb Cathedral Rock at sunset in Sedona
description: Iron-stained sandstone spires, a serious short scramble, and a town built around the belief that the rocks emit energy vortexes.

title: Walk among the saguaro at sunset
description: Saguaro grow only in the Sonoran, take 35 years to flower and 75 to sprout an arm. The tallest here are over 12m.

title: See the fossil logs at Petrified Forest
description: 225-million-year-old trees turned to quartz, plus a stretch of original Route 66. One of the very few national parks where dogs can join you on trails.

title: Drive the surviving stretches of Route 66
description: Decommissioned in 1985 and replaced by interstates, but long segments survive as business routes through towns the freeway bypassed.

title: Look into Meteor Crater
description: 1.2km wide and 170m deep, punched out 50,000 years ago and the first crater on earth proven to be from an impact. Apollo crews trained in it.

title: Wade The Narrows in Zion
description: Walking up the Virgin River between 300m walls that close to nine metres apart. Closed whenever flash flood risk is high - check daily.

title: Walk the chains up Angels Landing
description: A 500m spine with chains and drops on both sides. Permits have been required since 2022, by lottery, and the fatality count is in the teens.

title: Walk down among the hoodoos at Bryce Canyon
description: Not a canyon but an eroding escarpment holding the densest concentration of hoodoos on earth. The Navajo Loop takes you between them.

title: Walk to Delicate Arch for sunset
description: The arch on Utah's licence plates - 4.8km return over slickrock with no shade. Arches has held over 2,000 arches and loses one occasionally.

title: Watch sunrise through Mesa Arch at Canyonlands
description: For about twenty minutes at dawn the underside of the arch glows orange from light bouncing off the canyon below.

title: Drive the Burr Trail through Capitol Reef
description: A 160km wrinkle in the earth's crust called the Waterpocket Fold, and the least visited of Utah's five parks. Pick fruit in the Fruita orchards in season.

title: Wander the mushroom rocks at Goblin Valley
description: A valley of squat hoodoos you are actually encouraged to scramble over - rare in a landscape this fragile, and excellent for it.

title: Drive on the Bonneville Salt Flats
description: About 120 square kilometres of salt crust where land speed records have been set since 1912. Wet for much of the year - check before driving on.

title: Find Spiral Jetty on the Great Salt Lake
description: Robert Smithson's 460m basalt coil from 1970, submerged for thirty years and now high and dry as the lake shrinks - which is its own commentary.

title: Sled the gypsum dunes at White Sands
description: 275 square miles of white gypsum sand you can toboggan down. Dogs are allowed on leash almost everywhere here, unusually.

title: Watch the bat flight at Carlsbad Caverns
description: Hundreds of thousands of Brazilian free-tailed bats spiral out of the natural entrance at dusk. Walk in through the same hole rather than taking the lift.

title: Climb the ladders to the cliff dwellings at Bandelier
description: Ancestral Pueblo homes carved into volcanic tuff, occupied for four centuries. Wooden ladders take you up into the alcoves themselves.

title: Walk the adobe streets of Santa Fe
description: Founded in 1610 and the oldest capital in the US, with a building code that has kept the whole centre in adobe. Georgia O'Keeffe's museum is here.

title: Visit Taos Pueblo
description: Continuously inhabited for over 1,000 years - the oldest such community in the US, and still without electricity or running water by choice.

title: See the dishes at the Very Large Array
description: 27 radio dishes, each 25m across, moved along rail tracks into different configurations across a high desert plain. Contact was filmed here.

title: Drive Trail Ridge Road in Rocky Mountain National Park
description: The highest continuous paved road in the US, topping 3,713m, with eighteen kilometres above the treeline. Timed entry applies in summer.

title: See the Maroon Bells reflected at dawn
description: Reputedly the most photographed peaks in North America, and lethal to climb - the mudstone is so loose they are known as the Deadly Bells.

title: Sandboard the Great Sand Dunes
description: The tallest dunes in North America at 230m, against the Sangre de Cristo range, with a seasonal creek at their base you can float down in spring.

title: Tour the Cliff Palace at Mesa Verde
description: 150 rooms built into an alcove by Ancestral Puebloans around 1200 CE and abandoned within a century. Ranger-guided entry only, ladders included.

title: Drive the Million Dollar Highway to Ouray
description: 40km of US 550 over three passes with no guardrails and a sheer drop on the outside lane. Built on an 1880s toll road for the silver mines.

title: Look into the Black Canyon of the Gunnison
description: So narrow and deep that parts of the floor get 33 minutes of sunlight a day. The Painted Wall is the tallest cliff in Colorado at 682m.

title: Watch the Grand Prismatic Spring from the overlook
description: The world's first national park, sitting on an active supervolcano. The overlook trail beats the boardwalk for seeing the colours.

title: Watch wolves at dawn in the Lamar Valley
description: Wolves were reintroduced in 1995 after seventy years' absence, and this valley is where you have the best chance. Bring a spotting scope and get up early.

title: Wait for Old Faithful to go off
description: Erupts every 60 to 110 minutes and is predicted to within ten minutes - the most predictable big geyser anywhere, though not the largest.

title: Paddle Jenny Lake under the Tetons
description: The range rises 2,100m straight off the valley floor with no foothills at all, because the fault runs right along its base.

title: Walk the base trail around Devils Tower
description: The first US national monument, declared in 1906. Sacred to more than twenty tribes, who ask climbers to stay off voluntarily through June.

title: Drive the Going-to-the-Sun Road in Glacier
description: 80km over Logan Pass, only fully open for about ten weeks a year, and now requiring a timed entry reservation in peak season.

title: Walk the Highline Trail along the Garden Wall
description: Cut into a cliff along the Continental Divide, with a hand cable on the exposed opening section and mountain goats using the same path.

title: Walk the lava fields at Craters of the Moon
description: 1,600 square kilometres of basalt flows and lava tubes, last erupted about 2,000 years ago. Apollo astronauts trained here in 1969.

title: See Shoshone Falls at full flow
description: At 65m it is higher than Niagara, but irrigation takes most of the water for much of the year - spring runoff is the only time it performs.

title: Walk to Sawtooth Lake
description: A granite range with over 400 alpine lakes and no road through the middle of it, in one of the largest dark-sky reserves in the country.

title: Walk the Notch Trail in Badlands
description: A wooden ladder up a cliff face leads to a ledge over the White River valley, through eroded sediment laid down 75 million years ago.

title: See the faces at Mount Rushmore
description: Carved 1927-41 into a granite face in the Black Hills - land the Supreme Court ruled in 1980 was taken from the Lakota unlawfully.

title: Drive the Wildlife Loop in Custer State Park
description: A herd of around 1,400 bison, plus the Needles Highway with tunnels cut so tight they have to be measured before you drive them.

title: See the wild horses in Theodore Roosevelt National Park
description: The only national park named for a person, on the ranch land that turned him into a conservationist. Feral horses and bison on the loop road.

title: Walk into Santa Elena Canyon at Big Bend
description: 460m limestone walls with the Rio Grande running between them - the US on one bank, Mexico on the other, close enough to shout across.

title: Watch 1.5 million bats leave Congress Avenue Bridge
description: The largest urban bat colony in the world, roosting in bridge expansion joints and pouring out at dusk from March to October.

title: Queue for brisket in Texas Hill Country
description: Post oak, salt, pepper and about twelve hours. The best places sell out by early afternoon and the queue starts before they open.

title: Walk the River Walk and the Alamo
description: A flood control scheme from the 1930s turned into a river-level promenade, linking to four Spanish missions that are World Heritage listed.

title: Ride into Palo Duro Canyon
description: The second largest canyon in the US, 190km long and up to 240m deep, and almost nobody outside Texas knows it exists.

title: Wait for the Marfa lights
description: Unexplained lights reported since 1883, with a purpose-built viewing area on US 90 - and a town that became a minimalist art destination because Donald Judd moved in.

title: Kayak beneath the cliffs at Pictured Rocks
description: 60m sandstone cliffs on Lake Superior, streaked blue, orange and green by mineral seepage. The lake is cold enough to be genuinely dangerous.

title: Run down the dune climb at Sleeping Bear
description: A 137m sand bluff above Lake Michigan. Going down takes two minutes; coming back up takes most people close to an hour.

title: Cycle around car-free Mackinac Island
description: Motor vehicles have been banned since 1898, so everything moves by horse, bicycle or foot. The shore road is a flat 13km loop.

title: Portage a canoe through the Boundary Waters
description: More than 1,000 lakes linked by portage trails, with motors banned across most of it. You carry the canoe over your head between the water.

title: Walk into the Apostle Islands ice caves
description: Sea caves hung with icicles, reachable on foot only when the lake freezes solid enough - which has happened just a handful of times this century.

title: Take the architecture cruise on the Chicago River
description: The city rebuilt after the 1871 fire and invented the skyscraper doing it. The river was also reversed in 1900 so it flows away from the lake.

title: See your reflection in Cloud Gate
description: Anish Kapoor's 110-tonne stainless steel bean, welded from 168 plates with every seam polished away.

title: Ride the tram to the top of the Gateway Arch
description: 192m of stainless steel catenary curve, ascended in a tram of tilting five-person pods designed in two weeks in 1960.

title: See the exhibits at the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame
place: Rock and Roll Hall of Fame
description: In Cleveland because a DJ here popularised the term in the early 1950s. I M Pei designed the glass pyramid on the lakefront.

title: Go underground at Mammoth Cave
description: Over 685km mapped and still growing - by a wide margin the longest cave system known anywhere, and more than twice the next longest.

title: Follow the Kentucky Bourbon Trail
description: Around 95% of the world's bourbon is made in Kentucky, ageing in charred new oak in warehouses you can walk through and smell from the road.

title: Watch the synchronous fireflies in the Smokies
description: For about two weeks each June, one firefly species here flashes in unison. Access is by lottery, and it is worth entering.

title: Hear a songwriter round in Nashville
description: Broadway is the loud version; the Bluebird Cafe and the writers' rounds are where the songs actually get made, in rooms of ninety people.

title: Stand in the studio where Elvis recorded at Sun
description: A single small room where Elvis, Johnny Cash, Carl Perkins and Jerry Lee Lewis all recorded. Still a working studio at night.

title: Visit the National Civil Rights Museum at the Lorraine Motel
description: Built around the balcony where Martin Luther King Jr was killed in 1968. Room 306 is preserved exactly as it was that afternoon.

title: Follow the brass bands down Frenchmen Street
description: Where locals go when tourists go to Bourbon Street - live jazz in a dozen rooms within three blocks, most nights of the year.

title: Take a boat into the Atchafalaya swamp
description: The largest wetland and swamp in the US - bald cypress hung with Spanish moss, alligators, and a way of life built entirely on the water.

title: Walk the squares of Savannah
description: Laid out in 1733 around 24 public squares, 22 of which survive, under live oaks hung with Spanish moss.

title: See the wild horses on Cumberland Island
description: A barrier island reachable only by ferry, with feral horses on the dunes and the ruins of a Carnegie mansion in the maritime forest.

title: Paddle the mangroves in the Everglades
description: A river 100km wide and 15cm deep, and the only place where alligators and crocodiles share territory. Go in the dry season for the wildlife.

title: Drive the Overseas Highway to Key West
description: 180km over 42 bridges to the southernmost point in the continental US, built on the piers of Flagler's railway destroyed by a hurricane in 1935.

title: Snorkel the fort moat at Dry Tortugas
description: 113km west of Key West by ferry or seaplane - a vast unfinished brick fort on a sand key, with coral growing along the moat wall.

title: Watch a rocket launch from the Space Coast
description: Launch cadence is now high enough that a week here will usually catch one. The Saturn V hanging in the visitor complex is a real one.

title: Snorkel with manatees at Crystal River
description: The only place in the US where supervised in-water encounters with manatees are legal - they gather in the 22C springs when the gulf turns cold.

title: Walk the Battery in Charleston
description: Antebellum houses along the seawall, and the harbour where the Civil War began at Fort Sumter in 1861.

title: Drive the Blue Ridge Parkway in autumn
description: 755km of ridge road with no commercial traffic and a 72km/h limit. The colour moves down the mountain about 30m a day through October.

title: Climb the Cape Hatteras lighthouse
description: 257 steps up the tallest brick lighthouse in the US, on a barrier island so mobile the whole structure was moved 880m inland in 1999.

title: Walk the catwalk under the New River Gorge Bridge
description: A 24-inch catwalk 260m above the river, under the bridge deck. One day each October it is legal to BASE jump off the top.

title: Drive Skyline Drive through Shenandoah
description: 170km along the Blue Ridge crest with 75 overlooks. One of the few national parks where dogs are allowed on almost every trail.

title: Watch the pony swim at Chincoteague
description: Feral ponies swim the channel between islands each July, herded by the volunteer fire brigade who have run it since 1925.

title: Spend a day in the Smithsonian museums
description: Nineteen museums, all free, including Air and Space and the National Museum of African American History and Culture - the last needs timed passes.

title: Walk the memorials on the National Mall after dark
description: Lincoln, Vietnam and Korea are all open 24 hours and lit at night, when they are far quieter and considerably more affecting.

title: See the cherry blossom at the Tidal Basin
description: 3,000 trees given by Tokyo in 1912. Peak bloom lasts a few days and the date is forecast each year - it has been trending earlier for decades.

title: Tour Fallingwater
description: Frank Lloyd Wright cantilevered a house directly over a waterfall in 1935. Tours must be booked and sell out weeks ahead in autumn.

title: See the Liberty Bell and Independence Hall
description: Both the Declaration and the Constitution were debated in the same room. Free timed tickets, and the queue moves faster than it looks.

title: Walk Pickett's Charge at Gettysburg
description: Crossing the mile of open field the Confederate infantry walked into artillery fire in 1863 tells you more than any museum can.

title: Walk the High Line end to end
description: A disused elevated freight line turned 2.3km linear park through Manhattan's west side. Free, and dogs are not permitted.

title: Cross the Brooklyn Bridge on foot at dawn
description: The first steel-wire suspension bridge, opened 1883. Walk Brooklyn to Manhattan at first light and you will have the promenade to yourself.

title: Spend an afternoon in the Met
description: Two million works across 5,000 years, including an entire Egyptian temple moved stone by stone. Pick two wings and accept you will miss the rest.

title: Eat your way through a New York deli
description: Pastrami cured for weeks and steamed for hours, in rooms that have not been redecorated since the 1950s and are better for it.

title: Count the waterfalls at Watkins Glen
description: Nineteen waterfalls in three kilometres, on a stone path cut into the gorge that goes behind, under and over the water.

title: See all three falls at Letchworth
description: Called the Grand Canyon of the East - a 27km gorge with 180m walls and three major waterfalls, and hot air balloons over it in autumn.

title: Walk the Freedom Trail in Boston
description: 4km of red brick line through sixteen sites, from Boston Common to the Bunker Hill Monument, taking in most of the American Revolution.

title: Cycle the Cape Cod Rail Trail
description: 40km of flat former railway through pitch pine and cranberry bog, with the Atlantic dunes of the National Seashore at the far end.

title: See the first sunrise in the US from Cadillac Mountain
description: From October to March this is the first place in the continental US to catch the sun. Acadia is unusually dog-friendly for a national park.

title: Climb the iron rungs of the Beehive Trail
description: Iron rungs and narrow ledges bolted to a granite cliff, climbed in one direction only. Short, and not for anyone uneasy about exposure.

title: Eat a lobster roll on a working wharf
description: Maine lands most of the country's lobster. The argument over warm butter versus cold mayonnaise is genuine and locals hold firm views.

title: Drive the Kancamagus Highway in October
description: 55km through the White Mountain National Forest with no petrol, no shops and no phone signal - just sugar maples doing their thing.

title: Ride the cog railway up Mount Washington
description: The world's first mountain-climbing cog railway, running since 1869, up a summit that held the world land wind speed record at 372km/h for sixty years.

title: Chase the autumn colour through Vermont
description: Sugar maples turn earliest and brightest here, and the state runs a foliage tracker because the peak moves south about 50km a week.

title: Walk the Newport Cliff Walk past the mansions
description: 5.6km between Gilded Age summer houses and the Atlantic, with public access preserved by colonial-era shoreline rights the owners have fought for a century.

title: Cross the Edmund Pettus Bridge at Selma
description: Where marchers were beaten on Bloody Sunday in 1965, an event that moved the Voting Rights Act through Congress within months.

title: Drive the Natchez Trace Parkway
description: 715km following a path used for thousands of years, with no commercial traffic and sections of the original sunken trace you can walk.

title: Dig for diamonds at Crater of Diamonds
description: The only diamond-bearing site in the world open to the public where you keep what you find. Several hundred are found each year, most of them small.

title: Canoe on Moraine Lake in Banff
description: Rock flour suspended in glacial meltwater gives that colour. Private vehicles are now banned on the Moraine Lake road - shuttle only.

title: Drive the Icefields Parkway to Jasper
description: 232km past more than 100 glaciers between Lake Louise and Jasper - routinely called one of the great drives anywhere.

title: Stargaze in Jasper's Dark Sky Preserve
description: One of the largest accessible dark sky preserves in the world, with a decent chance of aurora on clear winter nights.

title: Walk the sea floor at Hopewell Rocks
description: The highest tides on earth, up to 16m. You walk on the ocean floor at low tide and kayak over the same spot six hours later.

title: Drive the Cabot Trail in autumn
description: 298km around Cape Breton's highlands, through Acadian and Gaelic communities, at its best when the maples turn in early October.

title: See polar bears at Churchill
description: Bears gather here waiting for Hudson Bay to freeze. There is no road in - you arrive by train or plane, and go out in a tundra buggy.

title: Visit the Watchmen sites on Haida Gwaii
description: Standing mortuary poles at SGang Gwaay, guarded by Haida Watchmen and deliberately left to return to the earth. Access is permitted and limited.

title: Take the boat under Horseshoe Falls
description: Around 2,800 cubic metres a second go over the Horseshoe. The Canadian side has the view; the boat gets you into the spray.

title: Walk the walled old town of Quebec City
description: The only walled city north of Mexico, founded 1608, and the most convincingly European place in North America.

title: Drive the Dempster Highway to the Arctic Ocean
description: Around 900km of gravel from Dawson City to Tuktoyaktuk on the Arctic Ocean. Carry two spare tyres - this is not an exaggeration.

title: Cycle the Stanley Park seawall
description: A 9km flat loop around a 400-hectare forest on a downtown peninsula, past totem poles and under the Lions Gate Bridge.

title: Cross the Capilano Suspension Bridge
description: 137m of swaying cedar plank 70m above a river gorge, first strung across in 1889. The free Lynn Canyon bridge nearby does much the same job.

title: Eat your way around Granville Island Public Market
description: An industrial sandbar turned market and artist quarter under a bridge, reached by tiny rainbow-coloured ferries that hold about twelve people.

title: Drive the Sea to Sky Highway to Whistler
description: 120km along Howe Sound with the water on one side and granite on the other, past Shannon Falls and the Stawamus Chief.

title: Climb the Stawamus Chief at Squamish
description: One of the largest granite monoliths in the world, climbed by chains and ladders to three summits above Howe Sound.

title: Hike to the Joffre Lakes
description: Three stacked glacial lakes in improbable turquoise. Day passes are required, and the park now closes for periods so Lil'wat and N'Quatqua Nations can harvest.

title: Ride the Peak 2 Peak gondola at Whistler
description: The largest ski resort in North America, linked by a gondola with the longest unsupported span in the world at over 3km between towers.

title: Storm-watch at Tofino in winter
description: People book rooms specifically to watch Pacific storms hit Long Beach. Surfing here happens year-round in a thick wetsuit.

title: Walk the rainforest trails in Pacific Rim National Park
description: Old-growth Sitka spruce and western red cedar on boardwalks over bog, with the West Coast Trail running south for 75 gruelling kilometres.

title: See the Butchart Gardens near Victoria
description: Built inside an exhausted limestone quarry from 1904 onward by the cement magnate's wife, and now a national historic site.

title: Look for the spirit bear in the Great Bear Rainforest
description: The Kermode bear is a white-coated black bear found almost nowhere else - maybe 400 exist. Access is through First Nations-led operators only.

title: Taste ice wine in the Okanagan Valley
description: Canada's warmest wine region, on a desert lake, and the source of most of the world's ice wine - pressed from grapes frozen on the vine.

title: Paddle to Emerald Lake in Yoho
description: Takakkaw Falls drops 254m in the same park, and the Burgess Shale here holds the best-preserved Cambrian fossils found anywhere.

title: Canoe on Lake Louise beneath the Victoria Glacier
description: Get there before seven or the car park is full by eight. In winter the lake freezes hard enough to skate and they carve an ice castle on it.

title: Walk on the Athabasca Glacier at the Columbia Icefield
description: The largest icefield in the Rockies, feeding three oceans. Markers along the approach road show where the glacier stood each decade - it is a sobering walk.

title: Ride the gondola at Banff for the Bow Valley view
description: Up Sulphur Mountain to a boardwalk along the summit ridge, with hot springs at the bottom that started the whole national park system in 1885.

title: See the dinosaur collection at the Royal Tyrrell Museum
description: One of the largest dinosaur collections in the world, in Drumheller, because the badlands around it are among the richest fossil beds anywhere.

title: Walk the hoodoos at Dinosaur Provincial Park
description: World Heritage listed, and more than 400 dinosaur skeletons have come out of it - many still lie exposed where they eroded out.

title: Visit Head-Smashed-In Buffalo Jump
description: Blackfoot peoples drove bison off this cliff for nearly 6,000 years. The interpretive centre is built into the hillside and told from their perspective.

title: Walk the Red Rock Canyon in Waterton Lakes
description: Joined to Montana's Glacier as the world's first International Peace Park, where prairie runs straight into mountain with no foothills between.

title: Go to the Calgary Stampede
description: Ten days of rodeo, chuckwagon racing and pancake breakfasts every July, with the whole city in boots. Running since 1912.

title: Hear the silence in Grasslands National Park
description: A Dark Sky Preserve of mixed-grass prairie with reintroduced bison and black-tailed prairie dogs, and almost no light or noise for a hundred kilometres.

title: Snorkel with beluga whales at Churchill
description: Around 57,000 belugas move into the Churchill River estuary each summer. They are curious enough to come and inspect a snorkeller.

title: Do the EdgeWalk on the CN Tower
description: A hands-free walk on a 1.5m ledge around the outside of the tower at 356m, tethered to an overhead rail. The tallest such walk in the world.

title: Swim at the Grotto on the Bruce Peninsula
description: A limestone sea cave on Georgian Bay with water clear enough to be mistaken for the Caribbean, and roughly ten degrees colder than it looks.

title: Canoe and portage through Algonquin Park
description: 2,400 lakes linked by portage, with wolf howls answered on organised August nights and maples that turn the whole park red in late September.

title: Skate the Rideau Canal in Ottawa
description: 7.8km of frozen canal used as a commuter route, with beavertail pastry stands on the ice. Warming winters mean some years it barely opens at all.

title: Cruise the Thousand Islands
description: Actually 1,864 islands in the St Lawrence, split between Canada and the US - one holds the shortest international bridge in the world.

title: Eat a smoked meat sandwich and a bagel in Montreal
description: Boiled in honey water and baked in a wood oven, the Montreal bagel is a genuinely different thing from the New York version - and locals will explain why.

title: Walk up Mont Royal for the city view
description: Designed by Frederick Law Olmsted, who also did Central Park. Sunday afternoons in summer bring the tam-tams - an open drum circle on the east slope.

title: Stand at the foot of Montmorency Falls
description: 83m, higher than Niagara, with a suspension bridge across the lip and a via ferrata up the cliff beside it.

title: Watch belugas in the Saguenay Fjord
description: One of the longest fjords in the world outside Scandinavia, with a resident and endangered beluga population, plus blue whales at the confluence.

title: Walk to Perce Rock at low tide
description: A 400m limestone wall with an arch through it, walkable from shore at low tide, with the world's most accessible gannet colony on the island beyond.

title: Photograph the lighthouse at Peggy's Cove
description: A working fishing village on granite scoured bare by glaciers. People are swept off the black rocks near the water most years - stay on the light-coloured stone.

title: Walk the painted waterfront at Lunenburg
description: A World Heritage town laid out on a 1753 British grid, still in its original wooden buildings, and home port of the schooner on the Canadian dime.

title: Visit Green Gables on Prince Edward Island
description: The farmhouse that inspired Anne of Green Gables, on an island of red sand cliffs where the book still drives a good part of the economy.

title: Walk on the earth's mantle at the Tablelands
description: Peridotite from the earth's mantle, forced to the surface by continental collision. So toxic to plants that it looks like Mars - and it helped prove plate tectonics.

title: Boat into Western Brook Pond
description: A landlocked fjord with 600m walls, reached by a 3km bog walk before the boat. The water is so pure it barely conducts electricity.

title: Watch icebergs drift past Iceberg Alley
description: Ice calved off Greenland glaciers 10,000 years ago, drifting down the Labrador Current. Locals chip it out for gin, and there is a public tracking map.

title: Stand among the puffins at Elliston
description: One of the closest land-based puffin viewing sites in North America - the birds nest on a stack a few metres from where you stand.

title: See the Norse settlement at L'Anse aux Meadows
description: The only confirmed Norse site in North America, occupied around 1021 CE - five hundred years before Columbus, and dated precisely by a solar storm.

title: Climb Signal Hill above St John's
description: Where Marconi received the first transatlantic wireless signal in 1901, above a harbour entrance called the Narrows and a street of painted row houses.

title: Drink the Sourtoe cocktail in Dawson City
description: A gold rush town with wooden boardwalks and a bar that drops a mummified human toe into your drink. The rule is your lips must touch it.

title: Fly over the Kluane icefields
description: Canada's highest peak and the largest non-polar icefield on earth, almost none of it reachable on foot. The flightseeing run is the only realistic way in.

title: Raft past Virginia Falls in Nahanni
description: One of the first four sites ever added to the World Heritage list, in 1978. Virginia Falls is twice the height of Niagara, and access is by float plane only.

title: Watch the aurora from Yellowknife
description: Directly under the auroral oval with a flat horizon and very dry winter air - statistically among the most reliable aurora viewing anywhere on earth.

title: Reach the floe edge on Baffin Island
description: The line where sea ice meets open water, travelled by snowmobile and qamutik sled with Inuit guides - narwhal, bowhead and polar bear all use it.

title: Swim in a cenote near Valladolid
description: Thousands of limestone sinkholes over a flooded cave system, sacred to the Maya and the peninsula's only natural fresh water.

title: Hear the Kukulkan pyramid echo at Chichen Itza
description: Clap at the base of El Castillo and the staircase returns a chirp said to imitate the quetzal. Twice a year a serpent shadow runs down the steps.

title: Ride El Chepe through Copper Canyon
description: A canyon system deeper and four times larger than the Grand Canyon, crossed by a railway with 37 bridges and 86 tunnels.

title: Eat your way through the Oaxaca markets
description: Seven moles, tlayudas, mezcal and chapulines - widely held to be the best regional cooking in Mexico, and it is not close.

title: Meet grey whales in San Ignacio Lagoon
description: Grey whales calve here and mothers routinely push their calves up to the boats to be touched - one of the strangest wildlife encounters anywhere.

title: Snorkel the reef at Akumal
description: Part of the Mesoamerican Barrier Reef, the second largest on earth, with green turtles grazing the seagrass close to shore.

title: Climb the Pyramid of the Sun at Teotihuacan
description: A city of over 100,000 people that was already ruins when the Aztecs found it and named it the place where gods were born. Summit access varies - check on arrival.

title: See the Aztec Sun Stone at the Museo Nacional de Antropologia
description: Widely rated among the best museums in the world - the 24-tonne Sun Stone, the Maya collection, and a courtyard fountain shaped like an umbrella.

title: Ride a trajinera through the canals of Xochimilco
description: The last surviving stretch of the Aztec canal and floating-garden system, with painted boats, mariachi for hire and the unsettling Isla de las Munecas.

title: Visit the Casa Azul, Frida Kahlo's house
description: The cobalt house in Coyoacan where she was born and died, kept as she left it. Tickets must be booked online and sell out days ahead.

title: See a lucha libre bout at Arena Mexico
description: Masked wrestling in a 16,000-seat cathedral of the sport, where the crowd's insults are half the performance. Friday nights are the big card.

title: Eat tacos al pastor from a spinning trompo
description: Lebanese shawarma technique applied to marinated pork, carved onto a small tortilla with pineapple flicked on top. Mexico City's defining street food.

title: Stand in the Zocalo and the Templo Mayor beside it
description: One of the largest city squares in the world, built directly over Tenochtitlan - the Aztec temple was found in 1978 by electricity workers digging a trench.

title: Climb the ruins at Uxmal
description: Puuc-style Maya architecture with an oval-based pyramid found nowhere else, and a fraction of the crowds at Chichen Itza an hour away.

title: Swim in the cenote at Ik Kil
description: An open cenote 26m down with vines hanging to the water. Busy - the quieter ones near Valladolid are better if you have a car.

title: Watch flamingos at Rio Lagartos
description: A biosphere reserve holding tens of thousands of American flamingos, plus a pink salt lagoon coloured by the same algae as Australia's Hutt Lagoon.

title: Walk the Paseo de Montejo in Merida
description: A boulevard of mansions built on the henequen fibre boom, in a city repeatedly ranked among the safest in the Americas.

title: See the Maya ruins at Tulum above the sea
description: The only major Maya city built on the coast, walled on three sides, on a cliff above a beach you can swim from. Go at opening to beat both heat and buses.

title: Float the canals at Sian Ka'an
description: A World Heritage biosphere where you drift down ancient Maya-dug canals wearing a life jacket, carried by the current through mangrove.

title: Dive the cenote at Dos Ojos
description: Part of one of the longest underwater cave systems on earth, with halocline layers where fresh and salt water meet and the view goes blurry.

title: Swim with whale sharks off Isla Mujeres
description: One of the largest whale shark aggregations in the world gathers off the Yucatan each summer - hundreds of animals feeding on tuna spawn.

title: Dive the underwater sculpture museum at MUSA
description: More than 500 concrete figures sunk off Cancun by Jason deCaires Taylor, built from pH-neutral marine cement so coral colonises them.

title: Boat through the Sumidero Canyon
description: Walls up to 1,000m high on the Grijalva River, with crocodiles on the banks and a moss formation shaped like a Christmas tree.

title: Reach the jungle ruins of Palenque
description: Maya architecture at its most refined, still half-swallowed by rainforest with howler monkeys overhead. Pakal's tomb was found intact under the main temple.

title: Swim the turquoise cascades at Agua Azul
description: Limestone-rich water over travertine terraces gives the colour - though it browns after heavy rain, so the dry season is the only time it lives up to the name.

title: Spend a few days in San Cristobal de las Casas
description: A highland colonial town at 2,200m, and the centre of Tzotzil and Tzeltal Maya life - the church at nearby San Juan Chamula is unlike anywhere else.

title: Stand on the terraces at Monte Alban
description: A Zapotec capital built by levelling an entire mountaintop around 500 BCE, looking out over three valleys.

title: See the petrified waterfall at Hierve el Agua
description: Mineral springs have built a rock formation that looks exactly like a frozen waterfall, with infinity pools at the top. Access is sometimes closed by local disputes.

title: Spend Dia de Muertos in Oaxaca
description: Comparsas through the streets and families keeping vigil in the cemeteries. It is a family occasion, not a festival - go quietly and ask before photographing.

title: Watch turtles nest at Mazunte
description: A former turtle slaughtering village that reinvented itself as a conservation centre after the 1990 ban - olive ridleys now arrive in mass arribadas.

title: Tour an agave distillery in Tequila
description: The blue agave landscape here is World Heritage listed. A plant takes seven years to mature, and only spirit made in this region may use the name.

title: Hear mariachi in Plaza Garibaldi's home town
description: Mariachi, tequila and charreria all originate in Jalisco. The Hospicio Cabanas here holds Orozco murals painted across its chapel ceiling.

title: Wander the tunnels and alleys of Guanajuato
description: A silver city built in a ravine, where the roads run through former river tunnels under the town and the houses are painted every colour available.

title: Watch the light on the Parroquia in San Miguel de Allende
description: A neo-Gothic pink church designed by a self-taught stonemason from postcards of European cathedrals, in a World Heritage colonial town.

title: Eat mole poblano where it was invented
description: Twenty or more ingredients including chocolate and several chillies, ground for hours. Also the home of chiles en nogada, eaten in the two months poblano chillies are in season.

title: Find the church on top of the Great Pyramid of Cholula
description: By volume the largest pyramid on earth, so overgrown the Spanish mistook it for a hill and built a church on the summit in 1594.

title: Swim at Playa Balandra near La Paz
description: A shallow turquoise bay you can wade most of the way across, with daily visitor caps to protect it. Frequently voted Mexico's best beach.

title: See El Arco at Cabo San Lucas
description: A granite arch at the very tip of the Baja peninsula, where the Sea of Cortez meets the Pacific. Reachable only by water taxi.

title: Dive with sea lions at Espiritu Santo
description: A World Heritage island in the sea Cousteau called the aquarium of the world, with a sea lion colony that plays with snorkellers.

title: Stand in the monarch butterfly forests of Michoacan
description: Hundreds of millions of monarchs arrive after a 4,000km migration and cover the oyamel firs so densely the branches bend.

title: Climb the pyramid of the Niches at El Tajin
description: 365 recessed niches, one for each day. The voladores still perform outside - five men descending from a 30m pole on ropes, a rite recognised by UNESCO.

title: Ride the Basaseachi trail in the Copper Canyon
description: Mexico's second-highest waterfall at 246m, in Raramuri country - the people known for running enormous distances in sandals cut from tyres.

title: Cross Lake Atitlan between the villages
description: A caldera lake ringed by three volcanoes and a dozen Maya villages, each with its own dialect and dress, connected only by boat.

title: Watch sunrise over the canopy from Temple IV at Tikal
description: Maya temples pushing up through rainforest, with howler monkeys roaring in the dark before dawn. The view from Temple IV was used as a rebel base in Star Wars.

title: Watch Semana Santa carpets in Antigua
description: Coloured sawdust laid into elaborate street carpets overnight, then destroyed by the procession walking over them at dawn.

title: Climb Acatenango to watch Fuego erupt
description: An overnight climb to 3,976m to camp opposite an active volcano that erupts every twenty minutes through the night. Cold, steep and unforgettable.

title: Swim the limestone pools at Semuc Champey
description: A natural limestone bridge carrying turquoise pools over a river that runs underneath it. The road in is genuinely rough and takes hours.

title: Dive the Great Blue Hole
description: A 318m-wide collapsed cave system 124m deep, with stalactites at 40m proving it was dry land during the last ice age. Advanced certification required.

title: Snorkel with rays at Hol Chan and Shark Ray Alley
description: A cut through the Belize Barrier Reef - the largest in the northern hemisphere - where nurse sharks and southern stingrays gather in waist-deep water.

title: Wade into the ATM cave at Actun Tunichil Muknal
description: You swim into a cave to reach Maya sacrificial remains calcified into the floor, including the Crystal Maiden. Cameras have been banned since one was dropped on a skull.

title: Soak in the hot springs under Arenal
description: A near-perfect cone that erupted continuously from 1968 until 2010 and is now dormant. The river running off it is naturally heated to bath temperature.

title: Walk the hanging bridges in the Monteverde cloud forest
description: Founded by Quaker pacifists who left the US in 1951. Resplendent quetzals nest here, and the forest is permanently inside the cloud layer.

title: Look for tapirs in Corcovado
description: National Geographic called it the most biologically intense place on earth - all four Costa Rican monkey species, plus tapir, jaguar and scarlet macaw.

title: Watch green turtles nest at Tortuguero
description: The most important green turtle nesting site in the western Caribbean, reachable only by boat or small plane through a network of jungle canals.

title: Zip-line through the Guanacaste canopy
description: Canopy zip-lining was invented in Costa Rica in the 1970s as a way for biologists to study the treetops, and became an industry by accident.

title: Watch a ship transit the Panama Canal locks
description: Around 14,000 ships a year lifted 26m over the isthmus by gravity-fed locks. The Miraflores visitor centre puts you level with the deck of a passing vessel.

title: Sail the San Blas islands with the Guna
description: 365 islands governed autonomously by the Guna, who set their own visitor rules and sell molas - reverse-applique panels sewn by hand.

title: Find the red frogs on Isla Bastimentos
description: Strawberry poison dart frogs that vary in colour island to island - a textbook case of populations diverging in isolation.

title: Volcano board down Cerro Negro
description: You walk up an active black cinder cone carrying a plywood board, then sit on it and slide down the ash at up to 90km/h.

title: Cycle between the two volcanoes of Ometepe
description: An hourglass island formed by two volcanoes rising out of a freshwater lake, with pre-Columbian petroglyphs on the lower slopes.

title: Look into the lava lake at Masaya
description: One of very few volcanoes on earth where you can drive to the rim and look directly down at moving lava. Visits are timed and short for good reason.

title: Learn to dive on Utila
description: Among the cheapest places in the world to get certified, on the Mesoamerican Reef, with whale sharks passing through much of the year.

title: Read the hieroglyphic stairway at Copan
description: 63 steps carrying around 2,200 glyphs - the longest Maya inscription known, and the finest stone carving anywhere in the Maya world.

title: Surf the point at El Tunco
description: Consistent right-hand point breaks over rock and black sand, on a coast that has quietly become one of Central America's best surf destinations.

title: Drive the Ruta de las Flores
description: 36km through coffee highlands and five colonial towns, with weekend food fairs and murals on nearly every wall in Ataco.

title: Ride a 1950s American car through Havana
description: Kept running for seventy years on improvised parts after the 1962 embargo cut off imports. Habana Vieja around them is World Heritage listed.

title: Ride through the tobacco fields of Vinales
description: Limestone mogotes rising straight out of a valley farmed by ox and plough, producing the tobacco that goes into Cuba's best cigars.

title: Walk the cobbled streets of Trinidad
description: A sugar-boom town frozen since the 1850s, with pastel houses, a live-music staircase every night, and steam trains into the Valle de los Ingenios.

title: Climb Dunn's River Falls
description: 180m of travertine terraces climbed hand-in-hand in a human chain, with the sea right at the bottom of them.

title: Walk the Blue Mountain Peak trail for sunrise
description: A 2am start to 2,256m, where on a clear morning you can see Cuba. The coffee grown on these slopes is among the most expensive in the world.

title: Visit the Bob Marley Museum in Kingston
description: His home and studio at 56 Hope Road, kept as it was, with the bullet holes from the 1976 assassination attempt still in the wall.

title: Swim with the pigs at Big Major Cay
description: Feral pigs that swim out to meet boats on an uninhabited cay. Nobody agrees how they got there, and overfeeding has killed several - follow the guides.

title: Dive the blue holes of Andros
description: The largest concentration of blue holes on earth, inland and offshore, beside the third-longest barrier reef in the world.

title: Watch humpbacks in Samana Bay
description: Thousands of North Atlantic humpbacks come here to breed each winter - one of the largest and most reliable gatherings anywhere.

title: Swim at Bahia de las Aguilas
description: 8km of undeveloped white sand inside a national park, reached by boat or a rough track - and protected from resort building so far.

title: Kayak the bioluminescent bay at Mosquito Bay
description: The brightest recorded bioluminescent bay in the world - dinoflagellates light up around the paddle. Go on a new moon, and never with sunscreen on.

title: Walk to La Mina Falls in El Yunque
description: The only tropical rainforest in the US national forest system, full of coqui frogs whose call is on every Puerto Rican recording ever made.

title: Walk the walls of Old San Juan
description: Blue cobblestones cast from iron ballast, and El Morro - a six-level fortress that held off Drake and stood for four centuries.

title: Swim with turtles off Carlisle Bay
description: A marine park with six shipwrecks in shallow water and a resident hawksbill turtle population, right off the capital.

title: Go down into Harrison's Cave
description: A limestone cavern toured by electric tram, with a 12m waterfall inside it and stalactites still actively forming.

title: Play mas at Trinidad Carnival
description: The carnival that soca and steelpan came from, and the template most Caribbean carnivals copy. J'ouvert starts at 4am covered in mud and paint.

title: Snorkel the Buccoo Reef and Nylon Pool
description: A protected reef with a waist-deep sandbar pool a kilometre offshore, named by Princess Margaret for water she said was clear as nylon.

title: Climb Gros Piton
description: 770m of volcanic plug straight up out of the sea, guided only. The two Pitons together are the most recognisable silhouette in the Caribbean.

title: Bathe in the sulphur springs at Soufriere
description: Billed as the world's only drive-in volcano - a collapsed caldera you drive into, with mud baths people coat themselves in.

title: Walk to the Boiling Lake in Dominica
description: The second largest hot lake on earth, at the end of six hours through the Valley of Desolation. The Nature Isle has 365 rivers and almost no beaches.

title: Swim with sperm whales off Dominica
description: Resident family groups live off this coast year-round, and Dominica is one of the only countries to license in-water encounters with them.

title: Stand in the shallows at Stingray City
description: Southern stingrays gather on a waist-deep sandbar in the North Sound, a habit that started when fishermen cleaned their catch there decades ago.

title: Snorkel the wall at Grace Bay
description: Repeatedly voted the best beach in the world, protected by a barrier reef so there is no seaweed and almost no swell.

title: Find the natural pool in Arikok National Park
description: A desert island of cacti and divi-divi trees bent permanently by the trade winds, with a rock-enclosed tidal pool reachable only by 4WD or on foot.

title: Walk Nelson's Dockyard at English Harbour
description: The only continuously working Georgian naval dockyard in the world, built by enslaved labour and now World Heritage listed.

title: Dive the underwater sculpture park off Grenada
description: The world's first underwater sculpture park, installed in 2006 to draw divers away from reefs damaged by Hurricane Ivan - and now a reef itself.

title: Squeeze through The Baths on Virgin Gorda
description: House-sized granite boulders forming tidal grottoes and passages you scramble and swim through between two beaches.

title: Follow the underwater trail at Trunk Bay
description: A marked snorkelling trail with underwater signs identifying the coral, in a national park covering roughly two thirds of St John.

title: Climb to the Citadelle Laferriere
description: The largest fortress in the Americas, built after independence by the world's first free Black republic to repel a French return that never came.

title: Dive off Atauro Island
description: Surveys here recorded the highest average reef fish diversity yet measured anywhere in the world, an hour by ferry from Dili.

title: Cross to uninhabited Jaco Island
description: Considered sacred, so nobody stays overnight - local fishermen take you across the strait at the far eastern tip of Timor-Leste.

title: Walk the Campuhan Ridge at first light in Ubud
description: A 2km grass ridge between two rivers, quiet before seven and unbearably hot after nine. The obvious first morning in Ubud.

title: See the Tegallalang rice terraces before the buses
description: Terraces watered by subak, a cooperative irrigation system run by temple priests since the ninth century and now World Heritage listed.

title: Get robbed by macaques in the Sacred Monkey Forest
description: Around 1,200 long-tailed macaques in a temple complex in the middle of town. They will take sunglasses, phones and anything shiny - leave it in the room.

title: Bathe in the holy springs at Tirta Empul
description: A purification ritual Balinese Hindus have performed since 962 CE. Sarong required, and the queue moves spout by spout in a set order.

title: Watch a Legong performance in Ubud Palace
description: Gamelan and masked dance in the palace courtyard nearly every evening - a living tradition rather than a tourist show, and cheap.

title: Climb Mount Batur for sunrise
description: A 2am start up an active volcano to watch the sun come up over Lombok. Local guides are effectively compulsory and the trail is enforced as such.

title: See the lake temple at Ulun Danu Beratan
description: A water temple appearing to float on Lake Beratan in the highlands, dedicated to the goddess of lakes and rivers. It is on the 50,000 rupiah note.

title: Walk between the Jatiluwih rice terraces
description: Far larger and far quieter than Tegallalang, with walking loops through working terraces rather than a viewpoint you photograph from a cafe.

title: Swim under Sekumpul Falls
description: Seven falls dropping into one gorge in north Bali, reached by several hundred steps and a river crossing. Widely rated the island's best.

title: Watch the sunrise gate at Lempuyang
description: The Gates of Heaven framing Mount Agung. The famous reflection is a mirror held under a phone by the photographer - everyone queues for hours for it anyway.

title: Snorkel the USAT Liberty wreck at Tulamben
description: A torpedoed US cargo ship pushed off the beach by the 1963 Agung eruption, now lying 30m from shore in water shallow enough to snorkel.

title: Explore the water palace at Tirta Gangga
description: Stepping stones across carp ponds in a royal water garden built in 1946, rebuilt after Agung buried it seventeen years later.

title: Watch the Kecak fire dance at Uluwatu at sunset
description: A sea temple on a 70m cliff, with a chanting circle of about seventy men performing the Ramayana as the sun goes down behind them.

title: Learn to surf the beach break at Canggu
description: Black volcanic sand, forgiving waves at Batu Bolong, and the centre of gravity for Bali's remote-working scene.

title: Surf or watch the reef break at Uluwatu
description: You paddle out through a cave in the cliff. A world-class left over shallow reef, and unforgiving of anyone who overestimates themselves.

title: Eat babi guling in a warung
description: Spit-roast suckling pig stuffed with turmeric, lemongrass and chilli - a ceremonial dish that most warungs sell out of by early afternoon.

title: Look down on Kelingking Beach from the cliff
description: A headland shaped like a dinosaur on Nusa Penida. The descent to the sand is a near-vertical scramble on bamboo rails - people are hurt on it regularly.

title: Snorkel with manta rays at Nusa Penida
description: Reef mantas visit a cleaning station here year-round. The swell can be heavy, and the boat ride out is not for anyone prone to seasickness.

title: Cycle the flat lanes of Nusa Lembongan
description: Seaweed farms, a yellow suspension bridge to Nusa Ceningan, and a fraction of the traffic of Penida next door.

title: Watch dawn break over Borobudur
description: The largest Buddhist temple on earth, built around 800 CE and abandoned for centuries under volcanic ash. Climbing to the upper terraces is now capped and guided.

title: Walk the temple complex at Prambanan
description: A ninth-century Hindu complex of towering candi, badly damaged in the 2006 earthquake and still under restoration. The Ramayana ballet runs here in the dry season.

title: See batik being drawn by hand in Yogyakarta
description: A sultanate city and the cultural centre of Java, where batik tulis is still drawn line by line with a wax pen rather than stamped.

title: Watch sunrise over Mount Bromo from Penanjakan
description: A smoking cone inside a caldera called the Sea of Sand, with Semeru erupting on the horizon behind it. A 3am jeep and genuinely cold at altitude.

title: See the blue fire at Kawah Ijen
description: Ignited sulphuric gas burning electric blue in the dark, above a turquoise acid lake. Gas masks are essential, and miners still carry 80kg of sulphur out by hand.

title: Ride to the crater rim at Tumpak Sewu
description: A 120m curtain of water in a horseshoe amphitheatre. The descent to the base is bamboo ladders and rope in permanent spray - hard, and slippery.

title: Eat your way through a Jakarta street food night
description: Nasi goreng, satay, martabak and kerak telor from carts that appear after dark, in a city of ten million with a food scene drawn from every island.

title: Look into the crater lake at Kawah Putih
description: A pale turquoise sulphur lake in a crater above Bandung, sitting at 2,400m so the air is cool and faintly acidic.

title: Track Komodo dragons on Rinca
description: The largest lizard on earth at up to 3m, found wild on five islands and nowhere else. Rangers carry forked sticks, which is less reassuring in person.

title: Climb Padar Island for the three-bay view
description: About 800 steps to a ridge overlooking three crescent bays, each with differently coloured sand. The most photographed view in eastern Indonesia.

title: Snorkel the pink sand at Komodo
description: Red organ-pipe coral fragments mixed through white sand give the colour - one of only a handful of genuinely pink beaches anywhere.

title: See the three coloured lakes of Kelimutu
description: Three crater lakes that independently change colour - red, green, black, turquoise - as their mineral chemistry shifts. Local belief holds they receive the dead.

title: Climb Mount Rinjani to the crater rim
description: 3,726m, usually done over three days with porters, to a crater holding a lake and a new cone growing inside it. Genuinely hard, and closed in the wet.

title: Snorkel with turtles off Gili Trawangan
description: Three car-free islands where transport is bicycle or horse cart, with green turtles grazing in water shallow enough to snorkel from the beach.

title: Surf the point at Kuta Lombok
description: A string of horseshoe bays with reef breaks for every level, and a fraction of Bali's crowds despite the airport being twenty minutes away.

title: Dive Raja Ampat, the richest reef on earth
description: Surveys record over 1,500 fish and 550 coral species - the highest marine biodiversity ever measured. Getting there takes two flights and a boat.

title: Climb Piaynemo for the karst lagoon view
description: A boardwalk and 320 steps to a platform above a scatter of mushroom-shaped karst islets - the view that defines Raja Ampat in photographs.

title: Dive the wall at Bunaken
description: A vertical coral wall dropping to well over 1,000m, with visibility routinely past 30m and turtles at almost every depth.

title: Muck dive the Lembeh Strait
description: Black volcanic sand rather than coral, and the best critter diving in the world - mimic octopus, hairy frogfish, blue-ringed octopus, all on one dive.

title: Attend a Torajan funeral ceremony
description: Funerals here last days and can happen years after death, with the deceased kept at home in the meantime. Visitors are genuinely welcomed - bring a gift and a guide.

title: Trek to see orangutans at Bukit Lawang
description: Sumatran orangutans in the wild on the edge of Gunung Leuser - one of only two places on earth where the species survives, and it is critically endangered.

title: Stay on Samosir Island in Lake Toba
description: The largest volcanic lake on earth, filling a caldera left by an eruption 74,000 years ago that may have nearly wiped out early humans.

title: Surf the Mentawai Islands
description: Reeled-off perfect reef breaks reached by charter boat from Padang, and among the most consistent waves anywhere in the world.

title: Island-hop the Karimunjawa archipelago
description: 27 islands in a marine park off Java's north coast, most uninhabited, reached by a slow ferry that puts most travellers off entirely.

title: Cross the Shibuya scramble at rush hour
description: Up to three thousand people cross at once when the lights change. The Starbucks window above it is the free viewing gallery.

title: Get to Senso-ji before the shutters go up
description: Tokyo's oldest temple, founded in 628. At six in the morning the approach is empty and the smoke from the incense cauldron is yours alone.

title: Eat sushi for breakfast at Toyosu
description: The tuna auction moved here from Tsukiji in 2018. Viewing from the deck is free; the sushi counters upstairs open at five.

title: Walk the Meiji Jingu forest in the middle of the city
description: A hundred thousand trees donated from across Japan in 1920 and planted to become a forest. It worked.

title: Drink in a Golden Gai bar the size of a cupboard
description: Two hundred bars in six alleys, most seating five or six people. Many charge a cover; the ones that welcome visitors say so on the door.

title: Look down on Tokyo for free from the Metropolitan Building
description: Two hundred and two metres up, no charge, and on a clear winter morning Mount Fuji is visible from the north tower.

title: See the Ghibli Museum in Mitaka
description: Tickets go on sale on the tenth of the month before and sell out the same day. No photography inside, deliberately.

title: Watch a sumo morning practice
description: Stables allow a small number of visitors to sit silently at the edge of morning training. Tournaments are only six times a year; this is not.

title: Walk from Yanaka cemetery through old Shitamachi
description: One of the few districts to survive both the 1923 earthquake and the firebombing, so the wooden houses and shopping street are original.

title: Walk up through the Fushimi Inari gates at dawn
description: Ten thousand vermilion torii up a mountain, each donated by a business. Open all night; go at five and you will meet almost no one.

title: Stand under the Arashiyama bamboo before seven
description: The sound of the stalks knocking together is on Japan's official list of soundscapes to preserve, and you can only hear it early.

title: See Kinkaku-ji reflected in its pond
description: Two floors covered in gold leaf, burned down by a monk in 1950 and rebuilt. Best after snow, which Kyoto gets a few days a year.

title: Sit in front of the rock garden at Ryoan-ji
description: Fifteen stones in raked gravel, arranged so you can never see all fifteen at once from the veranda. Nobody agrees what it means.

title: Walk the Philosopher's Path in cherry blossom
description: Two kilometres of canal lined with cherry trees, named for a philosopher who walked it daily to Kyoto University.

title: Eat kaiseki in a Kyoto machiya
description: A multi-course seasonal meal that is the formal end of Japanese cooking. Book weeks ahead; many places take no walk-ins.

title: Take part in a tea ceremony properly
description: Uji has grown the country's best matcha since the twelfth century. A full ceremony runs to a script and takes real time.

title: Bow to the deer at Nara Park
description: Twelve hundred wild sika deer that will bow back if you bow first. They are wild animals and will also take your map.

title: Stand under the Great Buddha at Todai-ji
description: Fifteen metres of bronze in what was the largest wooden building in the world until 1998, and is still enormous.

title: Eat takoyaki and kushikatsu in Dotonbori
description: Osaka's word for eating yourself broke is kuidaore, and this is where it happens. Never double-dip the kushikatsu sauce.

title: Cross the floating garden at Umeda Sky Building
description: Two towers joined by a doughnut-shaped roof deck 170 metres up, reached by an escalator through open air.

title: Climb the keep at Himeji Castle
description: The finest surviving Japanese castle, never burned or bombed, with six storeys of steep wooden stairs to the top.

title: Walk the Kumano Kodo pilgrimage route
description: A thousand-year-old pilgrimage through cedar forest, and one of only two pilgrim routes in the world with world heritage status.

title: Stay overnight in a temple on Koyasan
description: Sleep in a working monastery, eat shojin ryori and attend the dawn service. Okunoin cemetery at night is the reason to stay.

title: Climb Mount Fuji overnight for the sunrise
description: The official season is barely two months. Huts must be booked, and altitude catches out people who treated it as a walk.

title: See Fuji from Lake Kawaguchi in the morning
description: The mountain hides behind cloud most summer days. Winter mornings are clear, and the reflection in the lake is why people come.

title: Watch the snow monkeys bathe at Jigokudani
description: Japanese macaques that learned to sit in a hot spring. A 1.6-kilometre walk in through snow, and the monkeys ignore you entirely.

title: Walk the Azusa river at Kamikochi
description: A closed valley in the Northern Alps with no private cars, clear water and the Hotaka range standing over it.

title: See the thatched gassho houses at Shirakawa-go
description: Steep-roofed farmhouses built to shed four metres of snow, some three hundred years old and still lived in.

title: Walk the old merchant streets of Takayama
description: Dark timber sake breweries and morning markets in a mountain town that the modern railway reached late and lightly.

title: See Kenroku-en in every season
description: One of Japan's three great gardens. In winter the pines are hung with rope cones to stop the snow breaking them.

title: Walk the snow corridor on the Alpine Route
description: Snow walls up to twenty metres high, cut through each spring by ploughs, on a route crossed by cable car, bus and trolley.

title: See the lavender fields of Furano
description: Hokkaido's brief summer turns these hills purple for about four weeks. The Farm Tomita fields are the ones in the photographs.

title: Ski the powder at Niseko
description: Siberian air crossing the Sea of Japan dumps fifteen metres of dry snow a season here. It is why Australians learned to ski in Japan.

title: Look for brown bears in Shiretoko
description: A peninsula at the far north-east with one of the densest brown bear populations on earth, reached mostly by boat.

title: Walk the Sapporo Snow Festival sculptures
description: Two hundred snow and ice sculptures along Odori Park each February, some of them the size of buildings.

title: Walk the beech forest of Shirakami-Sanchi
description: The last large virgin beech forest in East Asia, world heritage listed, with almost no trails through the core.

title: See the gold hall at Chuson-ji
description: A twelfth-century hall covered inside and out in gold leaf, protected within a concrete shell, in the far north.

title: Take the boat through the pines of Matsushima bay
description: Two hundred and sixty pine-covered islets, ranked one of Japan's three great views since the seventeenth century.

title: Climb the thousand steps at Yamadera
description: A temple complex up a cliff, reached by 1,015 stone steps through cedar. Basho wrote a famous haiku here about the silence.

title: Stand in the Peace Memorial Park
description: The dome was left standing as it was on 6 August 1945. The museum next to it is unsparing and should be done slowly.

title: See the Itsukushima torii at high tide
description: The gate appears to float when the tide is in and you can walk out to it when it is out. Check the tide table before the ferry.

title: Cycle the art islands of Naoshima
description: A former industrial island turned over to Tadao Ando museums and a Yayoi Kusama pumpkin on the jetty.

title: Walk the Tottori sand dunes
description: Sixteen kilometres of coastal dunes up to fifty metres high, the largest in Japan, with camels for hire at the edge.

title: Visit Izumo Taisha, where the gods gather
description: The oldest shrine in Japan, where all eight million gods are said to meet each October. You clap four times here, not two.

title: Walk part of the 88-temple Shikoku pilgrimage
description: Twelve hundred kilometres around an island, walked in white with a staff. Most people do it in sections over years.

title: Eat tonkotsu ramen at a Fukuoka yatai
description: Open-air food stalls that set up on the riverbank each evening. Fukuoka is where the pork bone broth comes from.

title: Bathe in a Beppu onsen
description: More hot spring water comes out of the ground here than anywhere on earth except Yellowstone. Tattoo rules vary; ask first.

title: Walk to the ancient cedars on Yakushima
description: Cedars up to seven thousand years old in a moss forest that rains most days. The island Princess Mononoke was drawn from.

title: Look into the Mount Aso caldera
description: One of the largest calderas in the world with a live crater at the centre. Access closes without notice on gas readings.

title: Dive the Kerama islands
description: Water clarity here has its own name, Kerama blue, and humpbacks calve in the channel between January and March.

title: Snorkel with manta rays at Ishigaki
description: Manta Scramble is a cleaning station where mantas queue up. One of the most reliable manta sites in the world.

title: Ride a water buffalo cart on Taketomi
description: A coral-walled village of red-tiled roofs and sand streets, where the whole island is under a preservation order.

title: See the Emerald Buddha at Wat Phra Kaew
description: The most sacred image in Thailand, carved from a single block of jade and dressed by the king three times a year. Cover knees and shoulders.

title: Watch the sunset from Wat Arun
description: A seventy-metre prang encrusted with broken Chinese porcelain, best seen from the far bank as the light goes.

title: Eat your way along a Bangkok street
description: Chinatown after dark, where the woks come out onto the pavement. Follow the queues of locals rather than the signs in English.

title: Take a longtail through the Thonburi canals
description: The city was built on canals before it was built on roads, and on the west bank most of them are still there.

title: Cycle the ruins of Ayutthaya
description: The capital sacked by the Burmese in 1767, left as brick stupas and a Buddha head grown into a fig tree.

title: Climb to Doi Suthep above Chiang Mai
description: Three hundred and six steps flanked by naga serpents, to a gold chedi that has been there since 1383.

title: Spend a day at an ethical elephant sanctuary
description: Rescued working elephants, no riding and no bathing shows. The distinction between sanctuaries here matters; check before booking.

title: See the white temple at Chiang Rai
description: A privately built temple in white and mirrored glass, still unfinished, with a bridge over a pit of reaching hands.

title: Ride the 762 curves to Pai
description: A mountain road with a counted number of bends, to a valley town of hot springs and canyon ridges in the far north-west.

title: Climb the limestone at Railay
description: Seven hundred bolted routes on overhanging limestone, on a peninsula reachable only by longtail boat.

title: Kayak the mangroves at Ao Thalane
