description: Limestone karst rising straight out of mangrove channels, with the tide carrying you in and out. Quieter than Phang Nga.

title: Paddle into the hongs of Phang Nga Bay
description: Collapsed cave systems that form hidden lagoons inside the islands, entered lying flat in a kayak at low tide.

title: Sleep on a raft house at Cheow Lan Lake
description: Limestone towers out of an emerald reservoir, in a rainforest older than the Amazon. Hornbills at dawn, gibbons calling across the water.

title: Swim the Emerald Cave to Koh Muk
description: Eighty metres of swimming through a dark sea cave to a hidden beach inside a collapsed karst, with a rope to follow.

title: Cycle the Sukhothai historical park at dawn
description: The first Thai kingdom's capital, quieter and better preserved than Ayutthaya, with walking Buddhas in the lotus ponds.

title: Walk the old quarter's thirty-six streets
description: Each street was once a single guild's trade, and many still are. Crossing the road means walking slowly and not stopping.

title: Drink egg coffee in Hanoi
description: Invented in 1946 when milk was scarce: egg yolk whipped with condensed milk over strong coffee, served hot in a bowl of water.

title: Sleep on a boat in Bai Tu Long bay
description: The quieter half of Ha Long, with the same limestone towers and a fraction of the boats. Overnight is worth the extra day.

title: Be rowed through the caves at Trang An
description: Karst towers in flooded rice country, on a two-hour row through nine caves. The boatwomen row with their feet.

title: Ride the Ha Giang loop
description: Three hundred and fifty kilometres of mountain road along the Chinese border, through Hmong villages and the Ma Pi Leng pass.

title: Trek between the villages around Sapa
description: Rice terraces cut into the Hoang Lien Son mountains. Going with a local homestay host rather than a town agency changes the trip.

title: Go into the caves at Phong Nha
description: Home to Son Doong, the largest cave passage on earth. Paradise and Dark Cave are the accessible ones and are still vast.

title: Cycle the imperial citadel and tombs at Hue
description: The Nguyen capital, badly damaged in 1968 and slowly being restored, with emperors' tombs scattered along the Perfume River.

title: Ride the Hai Van Pass
description: Twenty-one kilometres over a spur of the Annamite range, with the weather often different on each side.

title: Have clothes made in Hoi An
description: A preserved trading port of Japanese, Chinese and French buildings, and several hundred tailors who will fit you in a day.

title: Canyon down the waterfalls at Da Lat
description: Abseiling into falls in the cool highlands the French built as a hill station. Choose the operator carefully; this one has a safety record.

title: Eat banh mi and pho on a Saigon street
description: The French left the baguette and the Vietnamese improved it. Pho in the south comes with a plate of herbs to add yourself.

title: Go down into the Cu Chi tunnels
description: Two hundred and fifty kilometres of hand-dug tunnel. A widened section is open to visitors and is still a tight squeeze.

title: Reach Cai Rang floating market at six
description: Wholesalers hang a sample of what they sell from a pole. By eight it is over, so the early boat is the only boat worth taking.

title: Watch the sun come up over Angkor Wat
description: The largest religious monument in the world. Buy the three-day pass; one day is not enough and the crowds thin after the first morning.

title: Find the faces at the Bayon
description: Two hundred and sixteen serene stone faces on fifty-four towers, at the centre of the walled city of Angkor Thom.

title: See the trees growing through Ta Prohm
description: Deliberately left partly unrestored, with silk-cotton roots prising the galleries apart. Go early; it is small and fills fast.

title: See the pink sandstone carving at Banteay Srei
description: Small, rose-coloured, and carved so finely it was long assumed to be the work of women. The best stonework at Angkor.

title: Visit Tuol Sleng and Choeung Ek
description: A school turned interrogation centre, and the field where its prisoners were killed. Take the audio guide and take your time.

title: Stay in the Cardamom Mountains
description: One of the largest intact rainforests in Southeast Asia, with community-run camps funding the rangers who patrol it.

title: Taste Kampot pepper at a plantation
description: Protected by origin, nearly wiped out under the Khmer Rouge, and now grown again on the same red soil by the same families.

title: Watch the alms round at dawn in Luang Prabang
description: Hundreds of monks collect rice at first light. Watch from a distance and quietly, or do not watch at all.

title: Swim in the Kuang Si pools
description: Turquoise limestone terraces below a fifty-metre fall, with a bear rescue centre on the walk in.

title: Balloon over the Vang Vieng karsts
description: The tubing-and-buckets era is over; the town now sells sunrise balloon flights over limestone towers and rice fields.

title: Look for Irrawaddy dolphins at Si Phan Don
description: The Four Thousand Islands where the Mekong braids out, with a handful of critically endangered dolphins in one deep pool.

title: Walk the Plain of Jars
description: Thousands of stone jars two thousand years old, in a province that was the most heavily bombed place on earth. Stay on the marked paths.

title: Cross the Petronas skybridge
description: The tallest twin towers in the world, joined at the forty-first floor. Tickets are capped daily and released online.

title: Climb the steps at Batu Caves
description: Two hundred and seventy-two rainbow steps to a limestone cave temple, guarded by a forty-three metre gold statue and rude macaques.

title: Eat char kway teow in George Town
description: Malaysia's food capital, where Chinese, Malay and Indian cooking have been arguing productively for two centuries.

title: Walk the mossy forest in the Cameron Highlands
description: Tea plantations the British planted, and above them a cloud forest where everything is covered in moss and pitcher plants.

title: Climb Mount Kinabalu
description: Four thousand and ninety-five metres, climbed overnight to reach the granite summit plateau at sunrise. Permits are capped and book out.

title: See orangutans at Sepilok
description: A rehabilitation centre for orphaned orangutans in Borneo, with a nursery viewing platform and feeding twice a day.

title: Dive Sipadan's wall
description: An oceanic island dropping six hundred metres, with barracuda tornadoes and turtles everywhere. Only 176 permits a day.

title: See the bat exodus at Mulu
description: Three million wrinkle-lipped bats spiral out of Deer Cave each evening in a ribbon that takes an hour to pass.

title: Snorkel with turtles at the Perhentians
description: White sand and green turtles an hour off the east coast, closed by the monsoon from November to February.

title: Walk the Supertrees at Gardens by the Bay
description: Vertical gardens up to fifty metres tall that vent the conservatories and light up twice a night. The skywalk between two of them is the view.

title: Eat at a hawker centre with a Michelin star
description: Hawker culture is UNESCO listed. Chicken rice for a few dollars, and the queue tells you which stall to join.

title: Walk the Southern Ridges tree-top bridge
description: Ten kilometres of connected parks and elevated walkways across the south of the island, with the wave bridge at the high point.

title: Look for otters along the Singapore River
description: Smooth-coated otters recolonised the city after the water was cleaned up, and now have their own celebrity families.

title: Take a water taxi through Kampong Ayer
description: A village of thirteen thousand people on stilts over the river, six hundred years old and still occupied.

title: Walk the canopy at Ulu Temburong
description: Untouched Borneo rainforest reached by longboat, with an aluminium tower taking you above the canopy.

title: Island-hop the Bacuit archipelago
description: Limestone islands with hidden lagoons you swim or kayak into. Tours are lettered A to D; C has the best lagoons.

title: Dive the Japanese wrecks at Coron
description: A dozen ships sunk by a US air raid in September 1944, most of them shallow enough to see without technical gear.

title: Paddle the underground river at Puerto Princesa
description: Eight kilometres of navigable river inside a mountain. Permits are capped daily and must be arranged in advance.

title: Walk the rice terraces at Batad
description: Two thousand years of terracing carved into the Cordillera by hand, in an amphitheatre you walk down into and back out of.

title: See the Chocolate Hills and the tarsiers
description: Over a thousand grass-covered limestone mounds that go brown in the dry season, with a tarsier sanctuary nearby.

title: Canyoneer down to Kawasan Falls
description: Three hours of jumping, sliding and swimming down a limestone canyon to a turquoise waterfall.

title: Surf Cloud 9 at Siargao
description: A hollow right-hand reef break over shallow coral, with a boardwalk out to a viewing tower above it.

title: Swim with whale sharks at Donsol
description: The interaction here is regulated and the animals are wild and unfed, which is not true of every whale shark site in the country.

title: Watch the sun rise over the Bagan plain
description: More than two thousand temples across forty square kilometres, built between the eleventh and thirteenth centuries.

title: See the leg-rowing fishermen on Inle Lake
description: Intha fishermen row standing with one leg wrapped round the oar, above floating gardens anchored to the lake bed.

title: Walk the platform at Shwedagon Pagoda
description: Ninety-nine metres of gold plate and several thousand diamonds, walked barefoot, best at dusk when the lamps come on.

title: See the Golden Rock at Kyaiktiyo
description: A gilded boulder balanced on the edge of a cliff, said to be held by a single hair of the Buddha.

title: See the Taj Mahal at sunrise
description: Twenty-two years and twenty thousand workers for one man's wife. The marble changes colour through the morning, which is the reason to be early.

title: Walk the red sandstone of Agra Fort
description: Where Shah Jahan was imprisoned by his son and spent eight years looking downriver at the tomb he had built.

title: Watch the Ganga Aarti at Varanasi
description: Fire, brass lamps and bells at dusk on the river, in one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities on earth.

title: Take a rowing boat along the ghats at dawn
description: Eighty-four ghats along the west bank, with bathing, laundry, cremation and prayer all happening within a few hundred metres.

title: Climb to Amber Fort above Jaipur
description: A hilltop fort of mirrored halls and stepped courtyards. Walk up rather than taking an elephant.

title: Look over the blue city from Mehrangarh
description: One of the largest forts in India on a 120-metre cliff, with the indigo-washed old town spread out beneath it.

title: Sleep in the dunes outside Jaisalmer
description: A living fort of yellow sandstone at the edge of the Thar, with camel treks out to the dunes for the night.

title: Row on Lake Pichola at Udaipur
description: Palaces on islands, hills behind, and the whole city built to be looked at from the water.

title: Find the stepwells of Bundi
description: Fifty ornate stepwells in a small blue town, almost none of them visited, and a palace Kipling wrote about.

title: Walk Old Delhi from the Jama Masjid
description: The largest mosque in India, then down into Chandni Chowk, which is the most concentrated street in the country.

title: See the Qutb Minar and the iron pillar
description: A 73-metre victory tower from 1193, beside an iron pillar sixteen centuries old that has never rusted.

title: Eat in the langar at the Golden Temple
description: A hundred thousand people are fed free every day by volunteers. Cover your head, remove your shoes, and take a turn washing up.

title: Drive over the Khardung La
description: One of the highest motorable passes in the world at over 5,300 metres. Acclimatise in Leh for two days before you attempt it.

title: Camp beside Pangong Tso
description: A saltwater lake at 4,350 metres that changes colour hour by hour and runs sixty per cent into Tibet.

title: Cross the Spiti valley
description: A cold desert of thousand-year-old monasteries between the Himalaya and Tibet, on roads that wash out most summers.

title: Raft the Ganges at Rishikesh
description: Grade three and four water where the river leaves the mountains, in the town the Beatles made famous in 1968.

title: Walk the Valley of Flowers in monsoon
description: Three hundred alpine species flowering at once, only during the rains, seventeen kilometres up from the road head.

title: Sleep on a Kerala backwater houseboat
description: Converted rice barges on nine hundred kilometres of lagoon and canal. The smaller canoes reach the channels the boats cannot.

title: Walk the tea estates at Munnar
description: Hills carpeted in tea to the horizon, and once every twelve years the neelakurinji flowers turn them blue. Next in 2030.

title: Watch the Chinese fishing nets at Fort Kochi
description: Cantilevered shore nets worked by teams of four, brought here by traders from Kublai Khan's court.

title: See the gopurams at Meenakshi Temple
description: Fourteen gate towers covered in thirty-three thousand painted figures, in a temple complex the size of a small town.

title: See the rock-cut caves at Ajanta and Ellora
description: Thirty-four temples cut down into solid basalt at Ellora, and Buddhist paintings at Ajanta lost in the jungle until 1819.

title: Walk to a living root bridge in Meghalaya
description: Bridges grown from rubber fig roots over decades by Khasi villagers, reached by three and a half thousand steps down.

title: Look for tigers at Bandhavgarh
description: One of the highest densities of Bengal tigers anywhere. Book the core zone and go on consecutive mornings.

title: Find the quiet beaches in south Goa
description: The north is developed; the south still has palm-backed crescents with fishing boats on them.

title: Walk the Kathmandu durbar squares
description: Three royal squares of pagoda temples across the valley, much of it rebuilt since the 2015 earthquake.

title: Walk the kora at Boudhanath
description: One of the largest stupas in the world, circled clockwise at dusk by Tibetan pilgrims turning the prayer wheels.

title: Trek to Annapurna Base Camp
description: Ten to twelve days into a glacial amphitheatre ringed by seven-thousanders, sleeping in teahouses the whole way.

title: Trek to Everest Base Camp
description: Twelve days up the Khumbu to 5,364 metres. The flight into Lukla is the part people talk about afterwards.

title: Paraglide over Phewa Lake at Pokhara
description: Thermals off the Sarangkot ridge with the Annapurnas behind, and one of the best places in the world to learn.

title: Look for rhinos in Chitwan
description: Greater one-horned rhino, gharial and occasionally tiger, in grassland and sal forest on the Indian border.

title: Climb to the Tiger's Nest
description: A monastery on a cliff ledge nine hundred metres above the valley, reached by a steep two-hour walk each way.

title: Watch a masked cham dance at a tsechu
description: Days of masked religious dance in a courtyard, attended by the whole town in their best kira and gho.

title: Walk the Bumthang valley temples
description: The spiritual heart of Bhutan, with the country's oldest temples and a daily fee that keeps visitor numbers low.

title: Climb Sigiriya rock at first light
description: Twelve hundred steps up a granite plug to a fifth-century palace, past frescoes and a gateway of giant lion's paws.

title: See the Temple of the Tooth at Kandy
description: A relic of the Buddha kept in a gold casket, shown only during the evening puja. The August perahera is the big one.

title: Ride the train from Kandy to Ella
description: Seven hours through tea country on a British-built line, with the doors open and everyone hanging out of them.

title: Climb Adam's Peak overnight
description: Five thousand steps by torchlight to a footprint claimed by four religions, and a shadow the mountain casts at sunrise.

title: Look for leopards at Yala
description: The highest density of leopards in the world, in scrub jungle where they sleep on the rocks in plain view.

title: Watch blue whales off Mirissa
description: The continental shelf comes close to shore here, so the largest animal that has ever lived passes within a few kilometres.

title: Walk the ramparts of Galle Fort at sunset
description: A Dutch colonial fort on a headland, still lived in, with the sea on three sides and cricket on the green.

title: Snorkel a house reef in the Maldives
description: Twenty-six atolls of coral rings. A resort with a good house reef gives you more time in the water than any boat trip.

title: Swim with manta rays at Hanifaru Bay
description: Currents funnel plankton into a small bay and up to two hundred mantas come to feed. Snorkelling only, and numbers are capped.

title: Stay on a local island rather than a resort
description: Guesthouses on inhabited islands have been legal since 2009, and cost a fraction of a resort. Local rules on dress apply.

title: Take a boat into the Sundarbans
description: The largest mangrove forest on earth, shared with India, and home to tigers that swim between the islands.

title: Walk the longest beach in the world
description: One hundred and twenty kilometres of unbroken sand on the Bay of Bengal, and almost entirely domestic tourism.

title: Walk the tea gardens at Srimangal
description: Bangladesh's tea capital, where they serve a seven-layer tea that stays separated in the glass.

title: See the Hunza valley in autumn
description: Apricot and poplar turning gold under seven-thousand-metre peaks, on the Karakoram Highway near the Chinese border.

title: Walk to Fairy Meadows below Nanga Parbat
description: A grass shelf facing the eight-thousand-metre Rupal face, reached by a jeep road with a reputation and then a walk.

title: See the Badshahi Mosque and Lahore Fort
description: Mughal building at its height, with a mosque courtyard that holds a hundred thousand people, facing the fort across a square.

title: Walk an unrestored stretch of the Great Wall
description: Jinshanling and Gubeikou are steep, crumbling and nearly empty, which Badaling is not.

title: Cross the Forbidden City north to south
description: Nine hundred and eighty buildings over seventy-two hectares. Tickets are capped daily and sold online with a passport number.

title: Walk the Temple of Heaven park in the morning
description: The park fills at seven with tai chi, ballroom dancing, choirs and card games. The temple is the excuse.

title: Stand in front of the Terracotta Army
description: Eight thousand figures, each with a different face, found by farmers digging a well in 1974. Pit one first, then three.

title: Cycle the Xi'an city wall
description: Fourteen kilometres of Ming wall, complete all the way round, wide enough to ride four abreast.

title: See giant pandas at Chengdu
description: Arrive at opening; pandas are active in the cool of the morning and asleep by ten.

title: Walk the blue lakes of Jiuzhaigou
description: Travertine-dammed lakes so clear you can count the fallen trunks on the bottom, ringed by autumn forest.

title: Walk Tiger Leaping Gorge
description: Two days along a high trail above the Jinsha river, between two mountains over five thousand metres.

title: See the Yuanyang rice terraces flooded
description: Thirteen hundred years of Hani terracing, at its best when flooded in winter and reflecting the sky.

title: Walk the sandstone pillars at Zhangjiajie
description: Three thousand quartz sandstone columns in the mist, and the glass bridge over the Grand Canyon nearby if you can face it.

title: Cycle the karst country around Yangshuo
description: The limestone towers on the back of the twenty yuan note, best seen from a bike on the Yulong river road.

title: See the Mogao caves at Dunhuang
description: Four hundred and ninety-two painted grottoes on the Silk Road, a thousand years of Buddhist art sealed up until 1900.

title: Walk the Bund at night
description: Colonial banking houses on one side of the river and the Pudong skyline on the other, floodlit until eleven.

title: Walk Bukchon Hanok Village
description: Six hundred years of tiled-roof houses between two palaces, still lived in, so keep your voice down.

title: Watch the changing of the guard at Gyeongbokgung
description: Entry is free if you wear hanbok, which you can hire on the street outside, and most people do.

title: Eat at Gwangjang night market
description: Mung bean pancakes and raw beef tartare at counters that have been in the same families for generations.

title: Look into North Korea from the DMZ
description: The Joint Security Area opens and closes with the political weather. Book a licensed tour; independent access is not possible.

title: Cycle the royal tombs of Gyeongju
description: A thousand years of Silla capital, described as a museum without walls, with grass burial mounds in the middle of town.

title: Climb Hallasan on Jeju
description: South Korea's highest peak at 1,947 metres, a shield volcano with a crater lake, on an island of lava tubes and haenyeo divers.

title: Ride to the top of Taipei 101
description: The fastest lift in the world when it opened, and a 660-tonne steel damper ball you can walk around near the top.

title: Walk Jiufen old street in the rain
description: A gold-mining town of red lanterns and tea houses on a steep hillside above the sea. Better wet and out of season.

title: Walk the marble gorge at Taroko
description: Nineteen kilometres of marble canyon cut by the Liwu river. Check for closures; typhoons and quakes shut trails regularly.

title: Cycle the East Rift Valley
description: A hundred and eighty kilometres between two mountain ranges, through rice and indigenous villages on Taiwan's quiet side.

title: Ride the Alishan forest railway to the sunrise
description: A narrow-gauge line built by the Japanese for cypress logging, now climbing through three climate zones to a sea of cloud.

title: Ride the Star Ferry across the harbour
description: Running since 1888 and still the cheapest and best way to see the skyline. Sit on the lower deck.

title: Walk the Dragon's Back ridge
description: Forty minutes from Central to a ridge trail over the south coast. Three quarters of Hong Kong is countryside.

title: Eat dim sum from a trolley
description: Old-style tea houses where you flag down the trolley and stamp your own card. Go before eleven and share a table.

title: Take the tram to Victoria Peak early
description: The Peak Tram has run since 1888. The free circular walk around the summit is better than the paid viewing deck.

title: Walk from the ruins of St Paul's to Senado Square
description: A Portuguese church facade standing alone after an 1835 fire, and a world heritage old town behind it.

title: Eat a Macanese egg tart and pork chop bun
description: Four centuries of Portuguese and Cantonese cooking crossed into a cuisine that exists nowhere else.

title: See the Gandan monastery in Ulaanbaatar
description: A twenty-six metre gold Buddha rebuilt in 1996, in the one monastery Stalin's purges left standing.

title: Stay in a ger with a herding family
description: The valley where Genghis Khan's capital stood. Staying with herders is the normal way to travel here, not a novelty.

title: Ride a camel over the Khongoryn Els
description: Singing sand dunes up to three hundred metres high in the Gobi, near the cliffs where the first dinosaur eggs were found.

title: See the eagle hunters of Bayan-Olgii
description: Kazakh hunters flying golden eagles from horseback in the far west, with a festival each October.

title: Skate at Medeu above Almaty
description: The highest Olympic-size ice rink in the world at 1,691 metres, where dozens of world records were set.

title: Walk the Charyn canyon
description: Eighty kilometres of red rock canyon, often compared to Arizona, three hours from Almaty on the Chinese border road.

title: See Lake Kaindy's sunken forest
description: Spruce trunks standing dead and upright out of a lake formed by a 1911 earthquake, preserved by the cold water.

title: Stand in the Registan at Samarkand
description: Three madrasas facing a square, tiled in blue, and the single most impressive thing on the Silk Road.

title: Walk the Shah-i-Zinda avenue of tombs
description: A narrow street of eleven mausoleums, each tiled differently, built over eight centuries.

title: Walk the old town of Bukhara
description: A working Silk Road city rather than a monument: trading domes, a minaret Genghis Khan spared, and a pool in the centre.

title: Sleep inside the walls of Khiva
description: A walled desert town preserved almost whole, small enough to walk around the ramparts in an hour.

title: Walk the Siq into the Treasury at Petra
description: A 1.2km slot canyon opens onto a facade carved into the rock face by the Nabataeans around 2,000 years ago. Go at opening, before the canyon fills.

title: Climb the 800 steps to the Monastery at Petra
description: Larger than the Treasury and far quieter, because most visitors stop before the climb. A tea shack at the top looks out over the Wadi Araba.

title: Sleep in a Bedouin camp in Wadi Rum
description: Sandstone and granite towers in red desert, run by Bedouin tribes who hold the tourism rights. Stood in for Mars in half a dozen films.

title: Float in the Dead Sea
description: 430m below sea level, the lowest land on earth, and about ten times saltier than the ocean. It is also shrinking by roughly a metre a year.

title: Walk the colonnaded street at Jerash
description: One of the best-preserved Roman provincial cities anywhere, buried by earthquake and sand until the 1920s - the oval forum is almost intact.

title: Walk the Dana Biosphere Reserve
description: Jordan's largest reserve, dropping 1,500m from highland to desert through four biogeographic zones, on a village-run conservation model.

title: Dive the Red Sea reefs at Aqaba
description: Jordan's only coastline, 27km of it, with reefs unusually resilient to bleaching and a deliberately sunk C-130 Hercules at 17m.

title: Go up the Burj Khalifa at sunset
description: 828m and still the tallest building in the world by a wide margin. Book the sunset slot weeks ahead - it is the only one that consistently sells out.

title: Ride a 4WD over the dunes on a desert safari
description: Dune bashing, sandboarding and a camp dinner in the Al Marmoom reserve. Genuinely rough - not a good idea straight after eating.

title: Haggle in the Dubai gold and spice souks
description: Reached by abra across Dubai Creek for about a dirham. Roughly ten tonnes of gold sits in the windows at any time, and the price is always negotiable.

title: Visit the Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque
description: Holds 40,000 worshippers, with the largest hand-knotted carpet in the world on its floor. Free, and modest dress is provided at the entrance.

title: See the rain of light at Louvre Abu Dhabi
description: Jean Nouvel's 180m dome filters sun through eight layered star patterns, casting a shifting pattern of light on the galleries below.

title: Ride the world's longest zip line at Jebel Jais
description: 2.83km at up to 150km/h, flown head-first off the UAE's highest peak. The mountain road up is itself worth the drive.

title: Swim and climb through Wadi Shab
description: A boat across, 45 minutes on foot, then three pools to swim before squeezing through a crack in the rock to a waterfall inside a cave.

title: Walk the Balcony Walk on Jebel Shams
description: A ledge path along the rim of Wadi Ghul, called the Grand Canyon of Arabia, ending at an abandoned village cut into the cliff.

title: Camp in the Sharqiya Sands
description: Dunes up to 100m in bands of orange and white, still grazed by Bedouin herders. You let tyre pressure down at the edge and drive in.

title: Sail a dhow through the Musandam fjords
description: Sheer limestone inlets called the Norway of Arabia, on a peninsula separated from the rest of Oman by the UAE, with dolphins in the channels.

title: Go to the Friday goat market at Nizwa
description: Livestock paraded in a ring before dawn buyers, beside a 17th-century fort with a round tower built to survive cannon fire.

title: Watch green turtles nest at Ras al Jinz
description: One of the most important green turtle nesting sites in the Indian Ocean, with guided night and dawn visits from a reserve on the easternmost point of Arabia.

title: See Salalah green during the khareef
description: The monsoon turns a desert province green for three months a year - waterfalls, fog and the frankincense trees that made this coast rich.

title: Walk the Old City of Jerusalem
description: One square kilometre holding sites central to Judaism, Christianity and Islam. It sits in East Jerusalem, which most of the world regards as occupied territory.

title: Climb Masada for sunrise over the Dead Sea
description: A fortress on a desert plateau where a Jewish garrison held out against Rome until 73 CE. The Snake Path takes about an hour in the dark.

title: Float on the Sea of Galilee
description: Actually a freshwater lake, and the lowest on earth. The surrounding hills hold Capernaum and the Mount of Beatitudes.

title: Walk the Bauhaus White City in Tel Aviv
description: About 4,000 Bauhaus buildings put up by architects who fled Europe in the 1930s - the largest concentration anywhere, and World Heritage listed.

title: See Banksy's Walled Off Hotel in Bethlehem
description: A hotel built facing the separation wall, billed as having the worst view in the world, beside the Church of the Nativity. Entry is via Israeli checkpoint.

title: Walk the excavations at Jericho
description: Tell es-Sultan has evidence of settlement going back roughly 11,000 years, which makes it a contender for the oldest continuously inhabited place on earth.

title: Float over Cappadocia in a balloon at dawn
description: Up to 150 balloons lift at once over volcanic fairy chimneys. Flights are cancelled for wind more often than people expect - allow spare mornings.

title: Go down into the Derinkuyu underground city
description: Eighteen storeys cut into soft tuff, capable of sheltering 20,000 people with livestock, ventilation shafts and rolling stone doors.

title: Stand under the dome of the Hagia Sophia
description: Built as a cathedral in 537, converted to a mosque in 1453, a museum in 1935 and back to a mosque in 2020. Its dome went unmatched for a thousand years.

title: Get lost in the Grand Bazaar
description: Around 4,000 shops on 61 covered streets, trading since 1461 and among the oldest shopping complexes still operating anywhere.

title: Walk barefoot on the terraces at Pamukkale
description: White travertine terraces built by calcium-rich springs over millennia. Shoes are banned to protect them, and the Roman city of Hierapolis sits on top.

title: Walk the marble street at Ephesus
description: One of the largest Roman sites in the Mediterranean, with the Library of Celsus facade and a theatre that seated 25,000.

title: Watch sunrise among the heads on Mount Nemrut
description: Two-metre stone heads toppled from their bodies on a 2,134m summit, built as a tomb by a king who declared himself a god.

title: See the carved pillars at Gobekli Tepe
description: Monumental stone circles raised around 9500 BCE - roughly 6,000 years before Stonehenge, and by people who had not yet started farming.

title: See the Nabataean tombs at Hegra
description: Saudi Arabia's first World Heritage site - 111 tombs cut by the same civilisation that built Petra, and visited by a fraction of the numbers.

title: Stand at the Edge of the World near Riyadh
description: A 300m escarpment on the Tuwaiq cliffs where the plateau simply stops and an ancient seabed runs to the horizon. 4WD access only.

title: Walk the mud-brick city at Diriyah
description: At-Turaif, the original seat of the Saudi state, built in Najdi mud-brick and World Heritage listed since 2010.

title: Eat and haggle in Souq Waqif
description: Rebuilt in the traditional style on a centuries-old trading site, with a falcon souq and hospital in the middle of it.

title: See the collection at the Museum of Islamic Art
description: I M Pei came out of retirement at 91 to design it, on its own island so nothing could ever be built against it.

title: Drive to the inland sea at Khor Al Adaid
description: One of very few places on earth where the sea reaches into the heart of a desert, on the Saudi border and reachable only by 4WD across dunes.

title: Stand among the columns at Baalbek
description: The largest Roman temple complex ever built, with foundation stones over 800 tonnes that nobody has fully explained the moving of.

title: Take the boat through the Jeita Grotto
description: Two limestone caverns stacked over each other, the upper holding the largest known stalactite in the world at 8.2m, the lower toured by boat.

title: Walk the harbour at Byblos
description: Occupied for around 7,000 years and a candidate for the oldest continuously inhabited city. The Greek name for it gave us the word Bible.

title: Find the Tree of Life in the Bahraini desert
description: A mesquite standing alone in the desert for around 400 years with no obvious water source, roughly two kilometres from anything else.

title: Walk the layers at Qal'at al-Bahrain
description: A tell holding 4,000 years of continuous occupation, from the Dilmun civilisation up to a Portuguese fort on the top layer.

title: Go up the Kuwait Towers
description: Three towers finished in 1979, clad in eight million enamelled steel discs, badly damaged during the 1990 invasion and rebuilt afterwards.

title: Walk down Main Street at the original Disneyland
description: The only park Walt Disney personally walked, opened in 1955 on a former orange grove. Two parks now, and the Anaheim original is still the smallest.

title: Do all four parks at Walt Disney World
description: Magic Kingdom, EPCOT, Hollywood Studios and Animal Kingdom across 100 square kilometres - roughly the size of San Francisco, and its own governing district.

title: Ride the Hogwarts Express between Universal's two parks
description: The train only runs if you hold a park-to-park ticket, and the view out the window differs depending on which direction you travel. Epic Universe opened in 2025.

title: Take the studio backlot tram at Universal Studios Hollywood
description: A working studio with a theme park attached rather than the other way round - the tram runs through sets still used for filming.

title: Ride every coaster at Cedar Point
description: Seventeen roller coasters on a sand spit in Lake Erie, and widely regarded by enthusiasts as the best coaster collection anywhere on earth.

title: Survive the coaster count at Six Flags Magic Mountain
description: Twenty roller coasters, more than any park in the world, including one that launches you to 160km/h in under four seconds.

title: Ride the Dollywood coasters through the Smokies
description: Repeatedly voted the best theme park in the world by industry awards, built around Appalachian craft, bluegrass and Dolly Parton's own foundation.

title: Eat the fried chicken at Knott's Berry Farm
description: America's first theme park, which grew out of a roadside berry stand and a chicken dinner restaurant that still has the longest queue on site.

title: Ride through the chocolate factory town at Hersheypark
description: Built in 1906 as a picnic ground for chocolate factory workers. The streetlights in town are shaped like Hershey's Kisses, and the whole place smells of it.

title: Ride the Leviathan at Canada's Wonderland
description: Canada's largest park, with more roller coasters than anywhere outside the US, built around an artificial mountain you can walk inside.

title: Float the underground rivers at Xcaret
description: An eco-archaeological park built over Mayan ruins, where you snorkel through cave rivers and finish with a three-hour show of Mexican regional dance.

title: See the castle at Disneyland Paris
description: Le Chateau de la Belle au Bois Dormant is the most elaborate of all the Disney castles, with a stained-glass gallery upstairs and a dragon in the dungeon below.

title: Ride the wooden coasters at Parc Asterix
description: France's home-grown answer to Disney, built around the comic books, and locally regarded as having far better roller coasters.

title: Work through the countries at Europa-Park
description: Germany's largest park and repeatedly voted the world's best, laid out as eighteen European countries with thirteen coasters between them.

title: Ride Taron at Phantasialand
description: Famously cramped, because the park cannot expand outwards - so it builds upward and through itself, producing some of the most intense theming anywhere.

title: Wander the fairy tale forest at Efteling
description: Older than Disneyland, opened in 1952 around an illustrated fairy tale wood, and still the most atmospheric park in Europe after dark.

title: Ride the wooden coaster at Tivoli Gardens
description: Open since 1843 in the middle of Copenhagen. Walt Disney visited twice and took notes; its 1914 wooden coaster still carries a brakeman on every train.

title: Visit Bakken, the oldest amusement park in the world
description: Operating since 1583, when a spring was discovered here and entertainers followed the crowds. Free to enter, and set in a royal deer park.

title: Ride Helix at Liseberg
description: Scandinavia's largest park, built on a hillside so the coasters run down natural terrain, and transformed into a Christmas market each December.

title: Ride Nemesis at Alton Towers
description: Planning rules capped ride height at the treeline, so the coasters were dug into the ground instead - which is why Nemesis runs through a trench.

title: Ride Shambhala at PortAventura
description: Six themed worlds on the Costa Daurada, with one of Europe's tallest coasters and a Ferrari Land next door.

title: Spend a day at Gardaland
description: Italy's largest park, on the shore of Lake Garda, with a SeaLife aquarium attached and a genuinely good pirate dark ride.

title: Ride Journey to the Center of the Earth at Tokyo DisneySea
description: DisneySea exists nowhere else and is widely held to be the most beautifully themed park ever built - a volcano at its centre that actually erupts.

title: Visit Super Nintendo World at Universal Studios Japan
description: The first Super Nintendo World anywhere, where a wristband lets you collect coins by punching blocks around the land.

title: Ride the coasters under Mount Fuji at Fuji-Q Highland
description: Several record-breaking coasters with Fuji filling the horizon, plus a haunted hospital attraction that takes about an hour to walk through.

title: Ride the Mystic Manor at Hong Kong Disneyland
description: The smallest Disney park, but home to Mystic Manor - a trackless dark ride built here because Chinese custom made a haunted house a poor fit.

title: Take the cable car over the headland at Ocean Park
description: Half marine park, half thrill park, split across a headland and joined by a cable car and a funicular through the rock.

title: See the largest Disney castle at Shanghai Disneyland
description: The Enchanted Storybook Castle is the biggest Disney has built and the only one belonging to no single princess. Opened 2016, and Tron runs here best.

title: Ride the T Express at Everland
description: South Korea's largest park, with one of the steepest wooden coasters in the world and a tulip festival that draws as many people as the rides.

title: Skate the indoor rink at Lotte World
description: The largest indoor theme park on earth, with an outdoor island section on a lake, connected by monorail and open whatever the weather does.

title: Spend a day at Universal Studios Singapore
description: Compact enough to do properly in one day, on a resort island reached by cable car, monorail or a boardwalk you can simply walk across.

title: Ride Formula Rossa at Ferrari World
description: The fastest roller coaster in the world at 240km/h, which is quick enough that riders are issued safety goggles before boarding.

title: Ride the Wild Mouse at Luna Park Sydney
description: Under the Harbour Bridge since 1935, behind a giant grinning face. The 1959 Wild Mouse is one of the last of its kind still running anywhere.

title: Eat currywurst standing up at a Berlin Imbiss
description: Invented by Herta Heuwer in 1949 from ration-shop ketchup and curry powder. Konnopke's has been under the U-Bahn viaduct since 1930.

title: Order a doner the way Berlin invented it
description: The doner in bread was a Berlin invention in the 1970s, not a Turkish one. Salad, sauce and grilled vegetables, which is the local difference.

title: Cycle the Schladitzer See and stop for a currywurst at Wolteritz
description: An open-cast lignite mine flooded into a lake north of Leipzig, with a flat ring road right around it. The beach cafe at Dorfstrasse 25, 04435 Schkeuditz does the currywurst you have earned by then.

title: Eat weisswurst before noon, as the rule demands
description: Made fresh each morning without preservatives, so tradition says they must not hear the midday bell. Sweet mustard, a pretzel, and you suck them out of the skin.

title: Buy a Dresdner Stollen at the Christmas market
description: Germany's oldest Christmas market, running since 1434, and the only place the protected Dresden stollen is sold by the people who bake it.

title: Drink Kolsch from a 200ml Stange until you say stop
description: The Kobes keeps replacing your small glass and marking your beer mat. Put the mat on top of the glass when you have had enough.

title: Eat a Thuringer Rostbratwurst off a charcoal grill
description: Protected by origin, at least 15cm long, and grilled over charcoal with mustard in a roll that is deliberately too small for it.

title: Eat a Fischbrotchen on the harbour
description: Pickled herring, onion and remoulade in a bread roll, eaten by the water. The northern answer to a sausage.

title: Eat a proper Wiener schnitzel, veal and hammered thin
description: If it is pork it is legally a schnitzel Wiener Art, not a Wiener schnitzel. Figlmuller's is pork and the size of the plate; Vienna forgives it.

title: Share a Salzburger Nockerl
description: Three baked peaks of sweetened egg white meant to look like the hills around the city. Made to order and collapses within minutes.

title: Scrape raclette off the wheel
description: Half a wheel of cheese held to the heat and scraped onto potatoes, gherkins and pickled onions. Winter food, and the Valais does it properly.

title: Eat Zurcher Geschnetzeltes with rosti
description: Veal in a cream and white wine sauce with a potato cake beside it, and the one dish the city claims outright.

title: Work through a Trappist beer list
description: Only a handful of breweries anywhere may call themselves Trappist and six of them are Belgian. Westvleteren is sold at the abbey gate by appointment.

title: Eat moules-frites in season
description: Mussels come from the Netherlands, the recipe is Belgian, and the season runs when there is an R in the month.

title: Eat raw herring the Dutch way, held by the tail
description: Hollandse Nieuwe lands in June, brined lightly and served with onion and pickle. Tip your head back and lower it in.

title: Order bitterballen with your beer
description: Crumbed balls of beef ragout, molten inside, served with mustard. The standard Dutch answer to a drink before dinner.

title: Eat bacalhau, one of the several hundred ways
description: Salt cod, imported from the Atlantic since the 1500s, and the country will tell you there is a recipe for every day of the year.

title: Take on a francesinha
description: Steak, sausage and ham between bread, buried in melted cheese and a beer-and-tomato sauce, with an egg and chips. One is a whole day.

title: Eat a full Irish with white and black pudding
description: Rashers, sausage, both puddings, egg, tomato and soda bread. The puddings are the part visitors skip and should not.

title: Eat Galway oysters straight from the bay
description: Native flat oysters, in season only when there is an R in the month, with a festival every September since 1954.

title: Eat pie and mash with liquor and jellied eels
description: A working London food older than fish and chips, down to a handful of shops. The green liquor is parsley sauce, not gravy.

title: Eat fish and chips at a proper seaside chippy
description: Fried in beef dripping in the north, cooked to order, salt and vinegar, eaten out of paper looking at the harbour.

title: Eat haggis, neeps and tatties
description: Sheep offal, oats and pepper in a casing. It is much better than its reputation, and there is a vegetarian version everywhere.

title: Try laverbread and cockles at Swansea market
description: Boiled seaweed rolled in oats and fried with bacon. Welsh breakfast, and an acquired taste worth acquiring.

title: Eat a canele fresh from the oven
description: Burnt-caramel crust, custard middle, baked in copper moulds lined with beeswax. Stale within hours, so buy them warm.

title: Eat bouillabaisse where the fishermen made it
description: Broth first with rouille and croutons, then the fish. A charter sets which species must be in it; anything cheap is not the real thing.

title: See a wheel of parmigiano cracked open
description: Dairies open for morning visits, and the wheels are tapped with a hammer to hear whether they have aged evenly.

title: Eat a cannolo filled to order
description: Sheep's-milk ricotta piped in as you order. Filled in advance the shell goes soft, and Sicilians will tell you so.

title: Eat paella where it comes from, at lunchtime
description: Rabbit, chicken and beans over wood, no chorizo, cooked at midday beside the rice paddies of the Albufera lagoon.

title: Eat fabada in an Asturian sidreria
description: White beans with chorizo, morcilla and pork belly. One bowl is lunch and most of the afternoon.

title: Eat souvlaki from a pita stand after midnight
description: Pork, tomato, onion, tzatziki and chips inside the pita, wrapped in paper. Ask for it apo ola and you get the lot.

title: Eat a Cretan dakos and drink raki with it
description: Barley rusk soaked in tomato with mizithra cheese, and the raki that arrives free at the end of every Cretan meal.

title: Eat pierogi at a milk bar
description: Bar mleczny are subsidised canteens left over from the communist era, still cheap and still serving the same dumplings.

title: Eat svickova with bread dumplings
description: Beef in a root vegetable cream sauce with cranberry and a spoon of whipped cream. The national dish, and rarely on tourist menus.

title: Eat goulash as the soup it actually is
description: Gulyas is a thin paprika soup, not the stew served abroad. The stew you are thinking of is porkolt.

title: Eat fuzi with truffle in Istria
description: Hand-rolled pasta with shaved truffle from the Motovun forest, in the Italian-influenced north-west.

title: Take a fika seriously
description: Coffee and a cardamom bun, sitting down, not at a desk. It is closer to an institution than a snack.

title: Eat fresh brown crab on the Bergen fish market
description: Landed that morning and dressed in front of you, on a quay that has traded fish since the 1200s.

title: Eat smorrebrod at lunchtime with a beer and a snaps
description: Open rye sandwiches, eaten in a set order from fish to meat to cheese. A lunch dish only, never dinner.

title: Eat a Karelian pie with egg butter
description: Rye crust around rice porridge, topped with butter mashed into boiled egg. Sold in every supermarket and eaten daily.

title: Eat an Icelandic hot dog with everything on it
description: Lamb in the sausage, crispy onions underneath, remoulade on top. Ask for eina med ollu and join the queue.

title: Eat sarmale with mamaliga and sour cream
description: Cabbage rolls stuffed with pork and rice, slow-cooked for hours, with polenta. Every family insists on their own version.

title: Eat banitsa for breakfast with ayran
description: Filo layered with white cheese and egg, sold hot from bakeries before work, with a salty yoghurt drink.

title: Eat cevapi with kajmak and onion
description: Small grilled minced-meat rolls in flatbread, with a clotted dairy spread the whole Balkans argues over.

title: Eat a balik ekmek off a boat at Eminonu
description: Grilled mackerel in bread, sold from boats rocking at the quay under Galata Bridge, with onion and lemon.

title: Sit at a ramen counter and order from the machine
description: You buy a ticket from a vending machine at the door and hand it over. Regional styles differ completely: tonkotsu, shoyu, miso, shio.

title: Eat okonomiyaki cooked on the counter in front of you
description: Cabbage batter cooked on a hotplate with whatever you choose in it. Osaka mixes it; Hiroshima layers it and adds noodles.

title: Eat yudofu at a temple restaurant
description: Simmered tofu in kombu broth, developed by Zen monks who ate no meat. Kyoto's soft water is the reason its tofu is famous.

title: Eat boat noodles by the bowl until you stack them
description: Tiny intensely spiced bowls, once sold from canal boats. You keep ordering and the empties pile up as the bill.

title: Eat khao soi in the north
description: Coconut curry noodles with crisp noodles on top, pickled mustard greens and lime. Northern Thai, and barely known abroad.

title: Eat bun cha at lunchtime in Hanoi
description: Grilled pork patties in a bowl of sweet-sour broth with cold noodles and herbs. A lunch dish; the stalls close by two.

title: Eat com tam, broken rice with grilled pork
description: Rice grains broken in milling, once the cheap leftover and now a Saigon breakfast in its own right.

title: Grill your own Korean barbecue with the banchan
description: The side dishes come free and are refilled. Wrap the meat in lettuce with ssamjang and eat it in one bite.

title: Eat bibimbap in the city it comes from
description: Jeonju's version uses beef tartare and rice cooked in beef broth. Mix it thoroughly; not mixing it is the mistake.

title: Eat a Sichuan hotpot and learn what ma la means
description: Numbing peppercorn as well as chilli heat. Order a split pot if you want to be able to taste anything afterwards.

title: Take yum cha slowly on a Sunday morning
description: Tea first, then trolleys. Tap two fingers on the table when someone pours for you; it means thank you.

title: Eat roujiamo and biangbiang noodles in the Muslim Quarter
description: A pork or beef flatbread sandwich claimed as the world's oldest, and a noodle whose character has 58 strokes.

title: Eat chaat in Old Delhi
description: Sweet, sour, hot and crunchy at once. Go where there is a queue and where the water is bottled.

title: Eat a South Indian thali off a banana leaf
description: Endless refills of rice, sambar, rasam and curd, eaten with the right hand. Fold the leaf towards you when you finish.

title: Eat Amritsari kulcha with chole
description: Stuffed bread baked in a tandoor until blistered, crushed with butter, and eaten with chickpeas at a roadside dhaba.

title: Eat assam laksa at a Penang hawker stall
description: Sour tamarind and mackerel broth with thick rice noodles, mint and pineapple. Nothing like the coconut laksa elsewhere.

title: Eat chilli crab with mantou to mop it up
description: Invented in Singapore in the 1950s. Order the fried buns; the sauce is the point and you will want to finish it.

title: Eat gudeg for breakfast in Yogyakarta
description: Young jackfruit stewed for hours in palm sugar and coconut until it goes mahogany. Sweet, and eaten first thing.

title: Eat Cebu lechon carved off the spit
description: Roasted whole over charcoal, stuffed with lemongrass and needing no sauce, which is the Cebuano boast.

title: Eat rice and curry with five or six sides
description: The everyday meal: rice, a curry, a mallum, a sambol and a papadam, mixed with your fingers on the plate.

title: Eat momos with tomato achar
description: Steamed or fried dumplings from the Newar kitchens of the valley, with a roasted tomato and sesame dip.

title: Eat plov cooked in a kazan the size of a table
description: Rice, lamb, carrot and whole garlic, cooked in the morning and sold until it runs out. Every city cooks it differently.

title: Eat khuushuur and drink suutei tsai
description: Fried mutton pastries and salted milk tea. Refusing the tea in a ger is worse manners than not finishing it.

title: Work through a Taipei night market
description: Oyster omelette, beef noodle soup, pepper buns. Stinky tofu is the test; the smell is far worse than the taste.

title: Eat fish amok steamed in a banana leaf
description: Freshwater fish in coconut and kroeung curry paste, steamed rather than boiled, which is what makes it Khmer.

title: Eat mohinga for breakfast
description: Catfish and banana-stem soup with rice noodles, sold from pavement stalls before seven. The national breakfast.

title: Eat ema datshi and mean it
description: Whole chillies stewed in yak cheese. Chilli is the vegetable here, not the seasoning, and the national dish is unapologetic.

title: Eat a full mezze until the table runs out of room
description: Twenty small plates before anything grilled arrives. Order less than you think and it will still be too much.

title: Eat hummus at a dedicated hummusia at breakfast
description: Warm, with olive oil, chickpeas and pita, eaten in the morning at a place that sells nothing else and closes by two.

title: Eat mansaf, and eat it with your right hand
description: Lamb cooked in fermented dried yoghurt over rice and flatbread. The national dish, and a communal one.

title: Eat baklava where it is taken most seriously
description: Forty layers, Antep pistachios, protected by origin. The city has a UNESCO listing for its cooking.

title: Eat machboos and luqaimat at an Emirati table
description: Spiced rice with meat, then dumplings in date syrup. Emirati food is surprisingly hard to find in Dubai unless you look.

title: Eat tacos al pastor cut off the trompo
description: Lebanese shawarma technique on pork with pineapple, brought by immigrants to Puebla in the 1930s. Two small tortillas, always.

title: Eat mole negro in Oaxaca
description: More than thirty ingredients including chocolate and several chillies, cooked over a day. Oaxaca claims seven distinct moles.

title: Eat gumbo and beignets on the same day
description: A roux the colour of a copper penny, and square doughnuts under an unreasonable quantity of icing sugar at Cafe du Monde.

title: Queue for Central Texas brisket at opening
description: Post oak, salt and pepper, twelve hours, no sauce. The good places sell out by early afternoon and the queue starts before opening.

title: Eat a slice folded, standing at the counter
description: Thin, wide, foldable, sold by the slice. The dollar slice is mostly gone but the fold is not negotiable.

title: Eat poutine after midnight
description: Chips, gravy and cheese curds that must squeak. If they do not squeak they are not fresh enough.

title: Eat a Montreal bagel straight from the wood oven
description: Boiled in honey water and baked over wood. Smaller, sweeter and denser than the New York kind, and open all night.

title: Eat jerk pork from a drum pan at Boston Bay
description: Where jerk was commercialised, cooked over pimento wood in a split oil drum. Scotch bonnet, allspice and smoke.

title: Order coffee the way Melbourne taught the world
description: The flat white, the magic and a serious argument about roasts. Italian and Greek migration built this, not a chain.

title: Eat a hangi cooked in the ground
description: Meat and vegetables steamed in an earth oven for hours. In Rotorua some are cooked using geothermal steam instead of hot rocks.

title: Sit with the lynching memorial in Montgomery
place: National Memorial for Peace and Justice
description: Eight hundred hanging steel columns, one for each county where a lynching took place, each carrying names. Allow the whole afternoon and expect it to be hard.

title: Swim off the quartz sand at Gulf State Park
description: Sand ground down from Appalachian quartz, so it stays cool underfoot in August, with 45km of trail behind the dunes.

title: Stand under a Saturn V at the Rocket Center
description: The largest collection of rockets anywhere, including a Saturn V lying on its side that is longer than a football pitch.

title: Bathe in a Hot Springs bathhouse
description: Forty-seven springs at 62 degrees plumbed into Edwardian bathhouses in the middle of town. The Buckstaff still runs the old way.

title: Paddle the Buffalo National River
description: The first national river in the country, protected undammed in 1972, beneath limestone bluffs 150 metres above the water.

title: Paddle into the Okefenokee at dawn
description: A peat bog the size of a county holding perhaps ten thousand alligators, with water stained black by tannin and overnight platforms out in it.

title: Walk the Atlanta BeltLine Eastside Trail
description: A disused rail loop being turned into 35km of park and path around the city. The Eastside stretch is finished, free and always busy.

title: Walk out onto the Ledge at Skydeck
description: Glass boxes cantilevered 412 metres up with nothing under your feet but Wacker Drive.

title: Follow what is left of Route 66 through Illinois
description: The original alignment still runs in pieces beside the interstate, through diners and neon that survived being bypassed in 1977.

title: Climb or walk the arches of Red River Gorge
description: More than a hundred natural sandstone arches, and some of the best sport climbing in the country on the same rock.

title: Stand at the Churchill Downs finish line
description: The Derby has run on the first Saturday in May since 1875. Outside race week the track and museum are quiet and cheap.

title: See the mill buildings full of art at MASS MoCA
description: Twenty-six former factory buildings in North Adams, holding art too big for a normal gallery, including a Sol LeWitt wall drawing retrospective on for decades.

title: Watch whales on Stellwagen Bank
description: A submerged sandbank that concentrates sand lance, and with them humpbacks that feed by blowing nets of bubbles.

title: Drive the North Shore to Grand Marais
description: A hundred and fifty miles along the largest freshwater lake in the world by surface area, with eight state parks and a waterfall in most.

title: Skate the Chain of Lakes when it freezes
description: The city ploughs rinks straight onto the lake ice and leaves them free and open. Locals treat it as a commute, not an outing.

title: Follow the Blues Trail through the Delta
description: Markers at the places the music actually came from, and juke joints in Clarksdale that still put a band on midweek.

title: Walk the siege lines at Vicksburg
description: Forty-seven days of siege ended on 4 July 1863 and split the Confederacy in two. The park road runs along both armies' earthworks.

title: Float the Current River
description: Spring-fed and cold enough to be a shock in August, through the first river system in the country protected as a national park unit.

title: Eat Kansas City barbecue at a burnt-ends counter
description: Burnt ends began as offcuts given away at the end of the brisket. Now people queue for them, which the original butchers would find funny.

title: Soak outdoors at Chico Hot Springs
description: An 1900 hot spring resort in Paradise Valley, open all year, and at its best when it is snowing on you.

title: Walk the Little Bighorn battlefield
description: White markers where the Seventh Cavalry fell, and since 2003 a memorial to the Lakota, Cheyenne and Arapaho who beat them.

title: Walk the Flume Gorge boardwalk
description: A 240-metre granite cleft with walls 27 metres high, walked on a boardwalk bolted into the rock since 1808.

title: Walk colonial Portsmouth and eat on the waterfront
description: One of the oldest towns in the country, small enough to cross in twenty minutes, with a working harbour still at the end of the street.

title: Watch synchronous fireflies at Elkmont
description: One of very few places on earth where fireflies flash in unison, for about two weeks in June. Access is by lottery.

title: See the Biltmore Estate and its grounds
description: The largest privately owned house in the United States at 16,000 square metres, with grounds laid out by the man who designed Central Park.

title: Stargaze in one of the darkest skies in the lower 48
description: Western North Dakota has almost no light domes at all. On a clear moonless night the Milky Way casts a shadow.

title: See the geographic centre of North America marker
description: A stone obelisk on a claim first made in 1931 by a rough calculation, disputed ever since, and cheerfully signposted anyway.

title: Walk to Old Man's Cave
description: A blackhand sandstone gorge of recess caves and waterfalls, cut into the one corner of Ohio the glaciers missed. Free.

title: See where the Wright brothers actually worked
description: The bicycle shop and the print works, not the beach at Kitty Hawk. Free, and the aircraft are at the Air Force museum up the road.

title: Watch WaterFire burn on the rivers
description: Eighty braziers lit on the water at sunset on scheduled nights and tended by crews in black boats. Free to watch.

title: Cycle around Block Island
description: Ten square miles reached by ferry, with 45 per cent of it under conservation and bluffs 45 metres above the Atlantic.

title: Walk the boardwalk under the champion trees
description: The largest old-growth bottomland hardwood forest left in the country, with some of the tallest trees in eastern North America. Free.

title: Hear Gullah Geechee history in the Lowcountry
description: The Penn Center was one of the first schools for freed people in the South, and the language and cooking of the sea islands are still their own.

title: Walk or ski the Stowe Recreation Path
description: Eight kilometres of paved path along the West Branch, free, and groomed for cross-country skiing once the snow comes.

title: Watch the sun set over Lake Champlain
description: The Adirondacks on the far shore turn the whole lake orange. The bike path along the waterfront runs out onto a causeway into the lake.

title: Visit the telescope in the National Radio Quiet Zone
description: Thirty-three thousand square kilometres where mobile phones and wifi are restricted by law, so a 100-metre dish can listen across the galaxy.

title: Raft the Gauley during the autumn dam releases
description: Twenty-two weekend days a year when the Summersville dam releases, turning the river into some of the hardest commercially run water in the country.

title: Eat at a Door County fish boil
description: Whitefish and potatoes boiled over an open fire, finished by throwing kerosene on the flames so the oil boils over the rim.

title: Eat cheese curds that squeak at the Dane County market
description: The largest producer-only farmers' market in the country, around the Capitol square. If the curds do not squeak they are not fresh.

title: Scramble to the summit of Old Rag
description: A granite scramble with real hand-over-hand sections near the top. Day-use tickets are capped and must be booked ahead.

title: Walk colonial Williamsburg out of season
description: The largest living history museum in the country. In winter the crowds go and the interpreters have time to talk properly.

title: Cycle the Tony Knowles Coastal Trail
description: Eighteen kilometres from downtown Anchorage along the Cook Inlet mudflats, with belugas offshore and the occasional moose on the path. Free.

title: Walk to the face of the Mendenhall Glacier
description: A glacier reachable on a city bus, with a free lakeside trail to a waterfall beside the ice. The visitor centre charges; the trail does not.

title: Walk the Wynwood murals
description: A warehouse district turned open-air gallery from 2009. The surrounding streets are free; only the walled courtyard is ticketed.

title: Drive Loop Road through Big Cypress at dusk
description: Forty kilometres of gravel through cypress swamp with alligators on the verge and barred owls calling. Free, and far quieter than the Everglades road.

title: Board the last wooden whaleship at Mystic Seaport
description: The Charles W Morgan, launched 1841, is the only wooden whaleship left afloat anywhere. The yard around her still builds and repairs by hand.

title: See the Gutenberg Bible at the Beinecke
description: Walls of translucent marble filter daylight onto a glass tower of books six storeys high. Free, and one of the strangest interiors in the country.

title: Drive the Litchfield Hills in October
description: White clapboard greens and covered bridges through the north-west corner, close enough to New York that people forget it is quiet.

title: See where Mark Twain wrote Huckleberry Finn
description: A nineteen-room Gothic house he designed himself and went bankrupt keeping. Harriet Beecher Stowe lived next door.

title: Take the boat around the Thimble Islands
description: An archipelago of pink granite outcrops off Stony Creek, some holding a single house, quarried for the stone in Grand Central Station.

title: Walk the Appalachian Trail along the Housatonic
description: The longest riverwalk section of the entire Appalachian Trail runs flat beside the water here for about eight kilometres. Free.

title: Watch the Coast Guard barque Eagle come in
description: A 1936 German-built square rigger taken as war reparations, still the training ship, and open to visitors when she is alongside.

title: Eat oysters where they are dredged
description: Long Island Sound oysters are farmed on beds worked since the 1800s, and the boats land at the same dock the restaurants sit on.

title: Walk the Rehoboth boardwalk out of season
description: A mile of boards, free, and in October the summer crowds are gone but the fudge shops are still open.

title: Cycle Cape Henlopen to the point
description: Second World War observation towers still stand in the dunes, built to spot U-boats off the Delaware Bay.

title: See the du Pont gardens at Longwood
description: A thousand acres of designed landscape around a house holding ninety thousand pieces of American decorative art.

title: Stand on the Green where Delaware ratified first
description: On 7 December 1787 Delaware became the first state, which is why the number one is on the number plates. The Green is unchanged and free.

title: Watch the shorebird migration at Bombay Hook
description: Tidal salt marsh on the Atlantic flyway, with a twelve-mile driving loop and hundreds of thousands of birds passing through in spring.

title: Paddle the Nanticoke River cypress swamp
description: The northernmost stand of bald cypress in the country, paddled between trunks in water the colour of tea.

title: Ride the Wilmington and Western steam train
description: A volunteer-run 1872 branch line through the Red Clay Valley, pulled by steam on scheduled weekends.

title: Eat scrapple for breakfast without flinching
description: Pork scraps and cornmeal, sliced and fried until the edges go crisp. A Mid-Atlantic breakfast that people either grew up with or refuse.

title: Kiss the bricks at the Indianapolis Motor Speedway
description: A metre of the original 1909 brick surface is left at the start-finish line, and winners kiss it. The track tour drives you round it.

title: Climb Mount Baldy at Indiana Dunes
description: A moving sand dune on the Lake Michigan shore with a steel mill on one horizon and Chicago on the other.

title: Walk Brown County State Park in October
description: The largest state park in Indiana, in hills the glaciers missed, and the best autumn colour in the Midwest outside New England.

title: Walk the modernist architecture of Columbus
description: A town of 50,000 with buildings by Saarinen, Pei and Roche, because one local industrialist paid the architects' fees for four decades.

title: Go underground at Marengo Cave
description: Found in 1883 by two children who climbed down a sinkhole with a candle. A national landmark, and still privately run.

title: Cycle the Pufferbelly and Rivergreenway trails
description: Forty kilometres of free path along three rivers through the middle of the city.

title: Watch the Little 500 bike race
description: Two hundred laps on a cinder track by student teams on identical single-speed bikes, run since 1951 and the reason Breaking Away exists.

title: Buy pie in northern Indiana Amish country
description: One of the largest Amish settlements in the country, with a Tuesday auction that has run since 1922 and buggies on the road shoulder.

title: Ride the Fenelon Place elevator
description: Ninety metres of cable car up a bluff, built in 1882 by a banker who wanted to get home for lunch. Three states visible at the top.

title: Drive the Loess Hills scenic byway
description: Wind-blown silt piled into hills up to sixty metres deep, a landform found at this scale in only one other place on earth, in China.

title: Find the covered bridges of Madison County
description: Six of the original nineteen survive, roofed to protect the timber trusses rather than the travellers. Free to visit, all of them.

title: Walk the bear and bird mounds above the Mississippi
description: Two hundred earthworks built between 1400 and 750 years ago, some shaped like animals and only readable from the bluff above.

title: Eat your way through the Iowa State Fair
description: The butter cow has been sculpted every year since 1911. Around eighty foods are sold on a stick, which is the point.

title: Walk the Amana Colonies
description: Seven villages founded in 1855 by German pietists who held everything in common until 1932, and still make the furniture and the wine.

title: Swim in the Iowa Great Lakes
description: One of only three blue-water glacial lakes in the world by the local reckoning, and where the whole state seems to go in July.

title: See the tulips at Pella in May
description: Three hundred thousand bulbs and a working Dutch windmill, in a town settled by Dutch dissenters in 1847.

title: Drive the Flint Hills Scenic Byway
description: The last large stand of tallgrass prairie on earth, saved because the ground is too rocky to plough. In June the grass is over your head.

title: Walk the Tallgrass Prairie National Preserve
description: Four thousand hectares with a bison herd, a stone barn from 1881, and nothing on the horizon in any direction. Free.

title: See the Garden of Eden folk art at Lucas
description: A Civil War veteran spent twenty-two years covering his log-cabin plot in concrete sculpture about labour and capital. He is buried in it.

title: Stand under Monument Rocks on the high plains
description: Chalk pillars twenty metres high left by an inland sea, on private land the owners let people visit free, down eight kilometres of dirt road.

title: Walk Boot Hill and the Santa Fe Trail ruts
description: Wagon ruts from the Santa Fe Trail are still visible west of town, cut deep enough by 1870 to survive a century and a half of weather.

title: Cycle the Arkansas River path in Wichita
description: Free paved path along both banks, past the Keeper of the Plains sculpture where the two rivers meet and fire pots are lit at dusk.

title: See real Mercury and Apollo hardware at the Cosmosphere
description: Hutchinson holds the largest collection of Russian space artefacts outside Moscow, and the actual Apollo 13 command module.

title: Eat steak at the Grand Central Hotel
description: Flint Hills beef eaten in the county it was raised in, on a brick main street ending at a French-roofed courthouse from 1873.

title: Eat crab with a mallet and Old Bay
description: Blue crab steamed and tipped onto brown paper. You are given a mallet and no cutlery, and it takes about three hours to eat properly.

title: See the wild ponies on Assateague Island
description: A feral herd on a barrier island, managed by fence into a Maryland group and a Virginia group. Camping here means securing your food properly.

title: Walk the Naval Academy and the state house
description: The oldest state house still in legislative use, where Washington resigned his commission in 1783. The dome is loblolly pine, no nails.

title: Sail a skipjack on the Chesapeake
description: The last commercial sailing fleet in North America, still dredging oysters under sail because the law requires it on certain days.

title: Cycle the Great Allegheny Passage
description: Two hundred and forty kilometres of former railway, joining the C&O towpath so you can ride from Pittsburgh to Washington without a road.

title: Ski or paddle at Deep Creek Lake
description: Western Maryland is high enough for real snow, so the same lake is a ski weekend in February and a swimming one in July.

title: Look for shark teeth under Calvert Cliffs
description: Miocene cliffs eroding into the bay, shedding fossil teeth onto the beach after every storm. A two-mile walk in from the car park.

title: Walk the Antietam battlefield at dawn
description: The bloodiest single day in American history, 17 September 1862. The farmland is kept as it was, which is what makes it land.

title: Watch half a million sandhill cranes on the Platte
description: Eighty per cent of the world's sandhill cranes stop on eighty kilometres of river each March. From a blind at dawn it is deafening.

title: See Carhenge
description: Stonehenge built from thirty-nine grey-painted American cars in 1987 as a memorial to the builder's father. Free, and open always.

title: Walk to the top of Scotts Bluff
description: A landmark on the Oregon Trail visible for a day's travel in either direction. Wagon ruts are still cut into the ground below it.

title: Drive the Sandhills Journey byway
description: Fifty thousand square kilometres of grass-stabilised dune, the largest such formation in the western hemisphere, and almost nobody on the road.

title: Walk the badlands at Toadstool Geologic Park
description: Mushroom-shaped rock in dry badlands, with a mammoth-kill site nearby and a campground of eight spots and no water.

title: See the big cats at Henry Doorly Zoo
description: The largest indoor desert and the largest indoor rainforest in the world, in a city that keeps quietly funding it.

title: See Chimney Rock from the trail route
description: The most mentioned landmark in overland trail diaries. It has eroded measurably since, so what you see is smaller than what they described.

title: Tank the Niobrara River
description: Floating a stretch of river in a livestock tank is a genuine Nebraska tradition, past two hundred waterfalls falling off the valley side.

title: Watch the autumn raptor migration at Cape May
description: The peninsula funnels migrating birds to its tip before they cross the bay. On a good September day the hawk count runs into thousands.

title: Paddle the cedar water of the Pine Barrens
description: Four thousand square kilometres of pine forest over an aquifer, with water stained red by cedar and iron, an hour from Philadelphia.

title: See a band at the Stone Pony
description: Open since 1974 and still a working room rather than a shrine, on a boardwalk that has been derelict and rebuilt twice since.

title: Walk to Mount Tammany at the Water Gap
description: A steep red-dot climb to a view straight down the notch the river cut through the ridge. Free, busy at weekends, worth an early start.

title: Cycle the Delaware and Raritan Canal towpath
description: Seventy kilometres of flat gravel towpath from Trenton to New Brunswick, past locks still worked by hand for the water supply.

title: Walk the Absecon Lighthouse and the boardwalk
description: Two hundred and twenty-eight steps up the tallest lighthouse in New Jersey, built in 1857 after a run of wrecks on the bar.

title: Eat a pork roll and look at Manhattan
description: The state argues about whether it is pork roll or Taylor ham depending on which half you are in. The skyline view is free either way.

title: Walk the undeveloped dunes at Island Beach
description: Sixteen kilometres of barrier island left as it was, with ospreys nesting and a maritime forest behind the primary dune.

title: Sit at the Oklahoma City National Memorial
description: One hundred and sixty-eight empty chairs, one for each person killed on 19 April 1995, nineteen of them small. The reflecting pool is free to visit.

title: Look for bison in the Wichita Mountains
description: Granite hills full of free-roaming bison, elk and longhorn, on one of the oldest refuges in the country. Free entry.

title: Walk the art deco of downtown Tulsa
description: Oil money built one of the densest collections of art deco in America between 1920 and 1935, and most of it is still standing.

title: Understand the Greenwood massacre where it happened
description: Black Wall Street was destroyed from the air and by mob over two days in 1921. The rebuilt district now carries the history openly.

title: Follow Route 66 across Oklahoma
description: More original alignment survives here than in any other state, including a stretch of the 1926 nine-foot-wide Ribbon Road.

title: Swim in the Beavers Bend clearwater
description: Cold clear water released from the bottom of a dam, in pine forest that feels like Arkansas rather than the plains.

title: Stand on Black Mesa, the highest point in Oklahoma
description: A lava-capped mesa at 1,516 metres in the far panhandle, thirteen kilometres return, with dinosaur tracks in the valley below.

title: Walk the Tallgrass Prairie Preserve at Pawhuska
description: Nineteen thousand hectares of restored prairie on the Osage Nation with around two thousand bison. Free, and the road through is gravel.

title: Board the USS Alabama at Mobile Bay
description: A South Dakota-class battleship that earned nine battle stars and was saved by Alabama schoolchildren collecting coins in 1964.

title: Walk Kelly Ingram Park and the Civil Rights Institute
description: The park where police turned dogs and hoses on schoolchildren in 1963, across the road from the church where four girls were killed that September.

title: Swim the falls at Little River Canyon
description: One of the few rivers in the country that runs its whole length on top of a mountain, cutting a gorge 200 metres deep. Free.

title: Watch the spring bird fallout on Dauphin Island
description: First land after a 900km Gulf crossing, so an April storm can drop thousands of exhausted songbirds into a few hectares of scrub.

title: Stand outside Little Rock Central High
description: Still a working school. Nine students walked in past a mob and the National Guard in 1957; the visitor centre opposite tells it plainly.

title: See the American art at Crystal Bridges
description: Safdie pavilions built over a ravine, holding American art from colonial portraits to Rothko, and free to enter permanently.

title: Walk to Hawksbill Crag
